open.title: 119 VALUES IN `data/tags.json` ARE READ BY NOTHING, AND THAT — NOT CLASS A — IS WHAT THE MUTATION ARTIFACT HAS BEEN HOLD
open.full: 119 values in `data/tags.json` are read by nothing, and that — not class a — is what the mutation artifact has been holding. measured 2026-08-22, release `6fb9ebd3b704`, 198,840 sheet entries. classes b and c of the sweep name a param the artifact carries and the simulator dereferences nowhere: it consumes the tag's membership and substitutes its own number. 130 carrier x tag x param rows, of which 11 are provenance metadata (see #325) and 119 are facts. ranked by share of corpus sheet entries: `move:protect / shieldsuser.{volatile,duration,bypassable}` and `stallcounterchecks.{counter,duration,deletesonfailure}` and `targetclass.{target,mustpressure}` at 67.75%; `move:fakeout / firstturnonly.{menudisable,whileactivemoveactions}` and `targetclass.*` at 12.44%; `item:lifeorb / damagemultall.costsperattack` at 10.69% — the row rediscovered the expensive way on 2026-08-21 after sitting here for sixteen days; `move:suckerpunch / needstargettoattack.needs` 7.11%; `move:flareblitz|wavecrash / recoil.readfrom` 6.42% and 5.74%; `move:matchagotcha / drain.{num,den}` 4.36% and `move:gigadrain / drain.{num,den}` 1.22%; `move:knockoff / readstargetitem.mult = 1.5` 2.65%; `move:lightscreen|reflect / halvesdamage.mult = 0.5` (deliberate and documented — the doubles engine uses 2732/4096); `item:lightclay|damprock / extendsduration.insteadof = 5`; `ability:regenerator / switchouttrigger.heal = 0.333`; `move:infestation / partialtrap.durationrange = [5,6]`. none of these is a behavioural defect on its own — the mutation moved nothing, so the engine's number currently agrees or does not matter — and that is exactly the problem: this is claude.md's *a derived artifact is not a fact until something compares it to its source* at 119 live sites, with no comparison anywhere. life orb is the proof that the failure mode is real rather than theoretical. the unit of work is a comparator, not 119 fixes: something that reads each of these params and asserts the engine's constant equals it, with a declared exception list carrying a reason (light screen's is written down already)

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MORPEKO SWITCH DIVERGENCE IS NOT A FORME-DATA GAP AND NOT AN ORDERING ONE — REFUTED WITH A CONTROL, AND THE REAL CAU
open.full: the morpeko switch divergence is not a forme-data gap and not an ordering one — refuted with a control, and the real cause is three defects on one shape. 2026-08-22, engine. #204 was routed on the premise that ten `event missing from medicham2` games name morpeko and that the missing forme rows caused them. three of the 40 cards in `data/divergence-turns.json` mention morpeko and one is the switch case, and it is not a switch order divergence at all: medicham2 emits no line for that slot, which is why the class is `event missing from medicham2`. speed, `comparepriority`, `switchin_order.js` and `data/switchin-order.json` are all irrelevant — those govern the order entry abilities resolve in, not which `|switch|` lines are emitted. refuted: the same board played against two releases identical but for the five forme rows gives byte-identical output. c1, engine — a non-permanent forme change is not reverted when the body leaves the field; measured off the bench, `ours morpeko-hangry` against `the authority morpeko`. showdown's `formechange` takes an `ispermanent` flag, hunger switch passes nothing, `clearvolatile` puts it back. c2, instrument — `game_differential.js` stamps `_switchkey` in `buildpair` (:2213) *precisely* so a rename cannot orphan a body (*“that body can never be switched to again”*), and `freshbodies` (:2362) — what every played game is built from — drops it: `buildpair ["morpeko","dragonite","espathra","garchomp"]` against `freshbodies [null,null,null,null]`. the resolver falls to `id(x.name)`, misses, answers `pass`. one fact, two construction paths, one of them fixed. sufficiency proved without editing the file: restamping from `onboundary` one boundary before the ask brings the subject back. c3, a different defect and said so — a mega is a permanent rename, so both engines hold `abomasnow-mega` while the ask still says `abomasnow`; the showdown branch (:3436) matches on `id(q.species.id)` and misses too, and the game throws rather than diverging. restamping does not clear it. over-fire control: the identical board asked as `{sw:'abomasnowmega'}` completes on both engines. nothing was fixed here on purpose — c1 is in `medicham2-browser.js` (owned by the damage-die agent that day) and c2/c3 are in `game_differential.js`, which is not in `sources` and is therefore read live by every run, so editing it moves a file under a measuring agent. full account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-formes.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: TESTING READS A CORPUS THAT MOVES UNDER IT, AND AN ARTIFACT RECORDS WHICH BYTES OF CODE MADE IT BUT NOT WHICH GAMES — WI
open.full: testing reads a corpus that moves under it, and an artifact records which bytes of code made it but not which games — will, 2026-08-17: "lets keep scraping games but for our testing purposes i just want a frozen corpus so it doesnt move". ops appends continuously and should keep doing so — `data/games.bo3.jsonl` and `data/games.ladder.jsonl` both moved at 21:01 on the day this was filed. what must stop moving is what testing reads. two channels leak today. (1) the differential's team pool, already filed as #81 wire 5 and stated in `engine/game_differential.js:4037` in its own words: *"`buildswarm` reads data/games.bo3.jsonl and data/games.ots.jsonl live, dedupes to distinct teams and picks by a stride over the matching set — so one appended game shifts the stride and changes which teams get played"*, with the note that both files moved during that wire's own test runs. the mitigation there asserts which team keys were picked, so a moved pool is visible afterwards; it does not stop the pool moving. `data/team-pool-frozen` already exists and is half the mechanism. (2) every `uses` count, which lives in `data/tags.json` and is regenerated from the live store — two divisions reported it independently on 2026-08-15 as *"~3,271 moved lines are `uses` counts following the store"*. the cost is measured, not hypothetical and not large: the metronome closet entry states 19 uses and the artifact reads 25, with nobody having edited either — the corpus grew underneath a typed number, which is this repository's signature failure in miniature. every impact ranking built on `uses` — the divergence work order, the bring guide, the mechanics priority — is therefore against a moving target at the margin. the second half is the provenance gap and it is the reason nobody noticed: an artifact carries an `engine_release` id saying which bytes of code produced it and nothing saying which games, so two runs can differ entirely in corpus and look identical in provenance. a corpus snapshot id belongs beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file. not a freeze of the store. ingest keeps running; testing reads a stamped snapshot. sequencing, deliberate: this lands before the mag refit and after the medicham gate closes. the refit is the run that most needs a stable corpus and is the one place where fitting against a moving target would be invisible; doing it before the gate closes would change the corpus definition under an in-flight measurement, which is the failure this row exists to prevent, committed while building the fix

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: SLEEP: THE DISTRIBUTION IS MODELLED CORRECTLY AND WHETHER THE DRAW IS ADDRESSED IDENTICALLY HAS NEVER BEEN CHECKED — RAI
open.full: sleep: the distribution is modelled correctly and whether the draw is addressed identically has never been checked — raised 2026-08-22, verification owed, no claim of breakage made. champions overrides `slp` and uses `this.sample([2, 3, 3])` (*"1/3 chance for a pokemon to wake up on turn 2"*) where mainline uses `this.random(2, 5)` giving 2, 3 or 4 — a different distribution and a different draw shape, since `sample` calls `random(3)`. our `sleep_turns_lost = 1 + 2/3` is exactly the expected value of `sample([2,3,3])`, one third times one plus two thirds times two, so the distribution half is right. what is unverified is the address: whether both engines consume the same number of draws at the same point, which is what decides every later die in a pinned game. reading mainline here is the documented way to be wrong. what would decide it: a pinned staged sleep on both engines printing the draw count and the address consumed, against the champions override read from the mod and cited by line. this row asserts nothing about a mechanic being wrong and deliberately carries no defect token in its cell: a row that overstates its scope costs a whole agent, which is more than the defect it names

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE CONFUSION SELF-HIT DRAWS A DIFFERENT INDEX FROM THE AUTHORITY, AND THE FORMULA IS RULED OUT AS THE CAUSE — OBSERVED
open.full: the confusion self-hit draws a different index from the authority, and the formula is ruled out as the cause — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 36; root cause unprobed. our formula is correct and documented: no stab, no type chart, no crit, no screen, no burn, sixteen sides at `85+r`, matching `getconfusiondamage` (`battle-actions.ts:1850`), with one gap declared rather than hidden — an `onmodifyatk` ability, so a burned guts body hits itself harder. the move is typed with the wildcard category, so no item or type boost can reach it; that hypothesis is ruled out. authority `108 -> 75` against our `108 -> 78` is 33 against 30, and `30/33 = 0.909` sits inside the 85-100% band, so it is a different index, not a different multiplier. note the authority takes two draws here — `randomchance(33,100)` for whether to self-hit, then `randomizer(damage)` — so a different order or category shifts every later die address too, and this may be an addressing defect rather than a damage one. what would decide it: pin the dice and print the index each engine selected for the same staged self-hit, plus the draw count consumed at that address. do not fold this into #333 until the index is read: one is a scheme and the other is an address

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: MOODY RAISES AND DROPS DIFFERENT STATS FROM THE AUTHORITY IN 8 OF THE 121 WHOLE-GAME DIVERGENCES, AND THE INSTRUMENT CAN
open.full: moody raises and drops different stats from the authority in 8 of the 121 whole-game divergences, and the instrument cannot say whether the two engines even share the die — filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. observed on `data/game-differential.json`, release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z: six causes in `-boost field 3` and two in `-unboost field 3`, e.g. `\|-boost\|p2a\|spa\|2 <> \|-boost\|p2a\|def\|2` and `\|-unboost\|p1a\|spa\|1 <> \|-unboost\|p1a\|spe\|1`. the magnitudes agree on every one — both sides chose a raise and a drop and only the stat identity parts — so this is selection, not clamping. both selection rules were read and they agree, which is what makes the draw the live question. the authority is `data/abilities.ts:2691-2719` (champions does not override `moody`): two `this.sample` draws, the first over boosts `< 6`, the second over boosts `> -6` excluding the stat just raised, both skipping accuracy and evasion, iterating `pokemon.boosts` in key order atk, def, spa, spd, spe. ours is `engine/medicham2-browser.js:23030-23042`: `_st=['at','df','sa','sd','sp']`, the same two predicates, `math.floor(rng()*l.length)`. same membership, same order, same number of draws, same mapping. two claims the wire-queue triage made for this mechanic did not survive a check. (1) its corroboration was the roster reading `fired-and-boards-differ`; `data/roster.abilities.json`, generated 2026-08-22t19:08:07z on the same release as the differential, now reads `fired-and-boards-match` with a second control (ice body) that found *"the two deltas differ on 28 leaf/leaves, which means at least one control is live on this fixture … 24 of 38 leaf/leaves survive both controls and the verdict is computed on those alone."* the differ was a live control. (2) *"under the middle arm's pinned dice both engines draw the same value at the same address"* is not supported: `engine/game_differential.js` wraps exactly three authority methods to derive a category — `hitstepaccuracy` → `acc`, `secondaries` → `sec`, `getdamage` → `dmg` — and a residual ability draw executes in none of them. the artifact agrees from its own side: every entry of `mid_void.unshared_address_shapes` is `acc`, `crit` or `dmg`. so this may be the instrument rather than the engine, which is the morpeko shape (#328, two of three causes were the harness), and no verdict is filed. what would decide it: print the address each side uses for the moody residual draw on one staged residual and compare — extend the category wrapper past the three `battleactions` methods, or publish that a residual draw is unshared. a stat-selection probe means nothing until that is answered settled 2026-08-23 by measure — it is the instrument, by construction, and nobody should touch the engine for it. the question this row asked (*does the residual draw share an address*) is answered inside `engine/game_differential.js` itself, read tonight: `mid_cats = ['acc', 'crit', 'sec', 'dmg', 'stall']` at :699, restated as the `out` set at :872, and the comment above it names what is deliberately excluded — *"the `any` bucket is every draw with no move in scope — target selection, sleep timers, multihit counts"* — with the measurement that justified the exclusion quoted beside it (95.2% identity on one sample and 37.0% on another from the same engine). moody's stat pick is `this.sample(stats)` on a residual (`data/abilities.ts:2704`) and is exactly that class, so the two engines draw independently and cannot agree except by luck. the signature agrees with the construction rather than merely being consistent with it: across all 8 games of the 2026-08-23 run the body, the protocol index and the magnitude are identical and only the stat name differs, over 5 distinct stat pairs with no repeated pattern — a rule defect picks the same wrong stat repeatedly. six of the 8 are carded and all six name scovillain; the two `-unboost field 3` members are inferred from shape, so if they are something else the instrument count is 6, not 8. the decision is `game_differential.js`'s, not engine's: either a new shared dice category, or a permanent and published exclusion from the rate. the original what-would-decide-it stands as confirmation and is still owed — print the address each side uses on one staged residual; the verdict above is a construction argument plus a signature, and not that print. declared 2026-08-24 by measure — `impossible to compare`, 8 games, and the scope is the pick and nothing else. the declaration is landed in `engine/quarantine.js` as kind `incomparable` under its own heading (*"the authority makes a random draw at an address this harness does not share … no defect, nothing to fix"*), printed with its own count and never summed with the `authority-wrong` kind. the clause moved `declared 5 → 13`, `undeclared 43 → 35` on 48 raw over 961 games; `diverged` and `declared` both still print, so the allowance is legible rather than absorbed. it is still red and nothing here could have opened it. the negative cases are the proof, not the positive one: nine mutations of this cause — each a real defect wearing the same shape — were injected through the shipping clause and every one fell through to undeclared: accuracy in the pool, evasion in the pool, `+3` instead of `+2`, `-2` instead of `-1`, our line unattributed, one of two occurrences unattributed, the authority attributing the boost elsewhere, the boost following that slot clicking a move, and a different slot on each side. selftest 108 passed / 0 failed. so a wrong magnitude, a wrong trigger rate or a pool containing accuracy or evasion is still a defect and is still counted — only which stat the die names is declared. the row is revisitable and says so: give the residual pick a named stream on both sides the way #290 did for `tie`, and this row must be deleted, not kept. still owed as confirmation: print the address each side uses on one staged residual — the verdict rests on a construction argument plus a signature (body, protocol index and magnitude identical across all 8, only the stat name differing, over 5 distinct stat pairs with no repeated pattern), and not on that print. the corner-arm half (*8 in `middle`, zero in either corner*) is derived from the pin code on this artifact and was measured independently on an earlier run. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-declared-moody-ties.md` declaration withdrawn 2026-08-25 by measure — the premise was refuted by measurement, and the thing this row called uncomparable was our own wrong address. nothing above is rewritten; it is dated and it stands as what was believed. what the declaration claimed: that a residual `sample()` "belongs to no named category on either side, so both engines take it off the generic `any` stream at an occurrence index each engine populates with its own unrelated draws" — therefore no shared address, therefore disagreement by construction, therefore nothing to fix. what was actually wrong: the `any` stream is shared; our half of the address was stale. the middle arm keys both engines' dice on `seed\|turn\|category\|move\|target\|nth`; the authority's `move`/`target` come off `battle.activemove`/`battle.activetarget` and it nulls both after every action (`sim/battle.ts:2828`) and again at the top of the residual (`:2810`, `clearactivemove(true)`, which runs before `fieldevent('residual')` and therefore before moody draws — both call sites read at the line, 2026-08-25). `engine/medicham2-browser.js` wrote `mid_move`/`mid_tgt` at the top of each action and never cleared them, so every end-of-turn die was addressed with a move name that had already finished: `authority 20260813\|1\|any\|-\|-\|0` against `this engine 20260813\|1\|any\|curse\|p20\|0`. two addresses that cannot match are two independent dice — a private coin because the address was ours and it was wrong, not because the authority's draw is unaddressable. the evidence, derived from the committed artifacts rather than recalled — same 961 games, same frozen pool, `wholegameclause` run over each with only the staleness stamp normalised: `0447cd1` (pre-fix, release `ffdec64bed0c`) 35 raw, declared 13 = incomparable 8 + authority-wrong 5, undeclared 22; `382e998` (post-fix, release `cbf345e56bc0`) 28 raw, declared 5 = incomparable 0 + authority-wrong 5, undeclared 23; `65a9c5c` (head, release `359b51b61d83`) identical to the post-fix figures. the eight games were seven causes — 6 x `-boost field 3`, 2 x `-unboost field 3` — and after the address fix zero games carry either shape. six stopped diverging outright; two now part on a different cause (`\|-immune\|p1a <> \|-miss\|p2b\|p1a`, and `\|switch\|p1a\|krookodile <> \|detailschange\|p1b\|charizardmegay`), so the exemption had been sheltering two real divergences that nothing could see while it stood. the engine change is engine's, in `midclearactivemove()`, with `medi_active_move_sticky=1` restoring the leak and stamping `medfails.activemovestickyrestored` so the red is reproducible rather than remembered. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-25-board-material-3.md` (engine) and `docs/_reports/2026-08-25-moody-undeclared.md` (this withdrawal). the row's own owed item is what killed it. this row said twice, in its own words, that the address print was *"still owed as confirmation"* and that the verdict rested on *"a construction argument plus a signature, and not on that print"*. the print was finally taken, and it refuted the verdict rather than confirming it. it also said the row must be deleted, not kept if the residual draw were ever given a shared stream; the stream was already shared and the row is duly withdrawn. what is not in dispute and never was: moody's rule. the authority takes two `sample()` draws over the five main stats only (`data/abilities.ts:2691-2716`, both loops `continue` on accuracy and evasion) and this engine implements that. what landed in code: the `incomparable` row is removed from `declared_divergence` in `engine/quarantine.js`, together with the two helpers that had no other caller, and replaced by a withdrawal note where the row stood. the nine negative mutations it used to be proven against are now simply the default — every one of them is undeclared — and a red ratchet asserts that a moody-shaped stat-pick divergence is undeclared and holds the gate shut, so re-adding the exemption goes red. the `incomparable` kind survives with no live row, and the two kinds are still proven to print apart on a synthetic pushed row rather than a shipping one. selftest 100 passed, 0 failed. the pattern, which is the part worth keeping: this is the fourth "nothing to fix here" in three days that turned out to be real — speed ties, tailwind twice, now moody's stat pick. in every case the reasoning was plausible and cited a line, and in every case the mechanism itself was never independently checked. a declaration is only as good as its mechanism, and a mechanism nobody re-derived is a guess wearing a citation.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A `\|switch\|` LINE IS ORDERED BY THE DEPARTING BODY'S SPEED IN THE AUTHORITY, AND NOTHING PUBLISHES WHETHER WE AGREE —
open.full: a `\|switch\|` line is ordered by the departing body's speed in the authority, and nothing publishes whether we agree — 3 of the 121, filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. causes (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `ordering :: \|switch\|p1b\|whimsicott,l50\|h/h <> \|switch\|p1a\|alakazam,l50\|h/h` (turn 2, a same-side double switch), `\|switch\|p1a\|staraptor <> \|switch\|p2a\|incineroar`, `\|switch\|p1a\|palafin <> \|move\|p2b\|helpinghand`. the authority's key is derived and verified line by line: `sim/battle-queue.ts:270` `if (!deferpriority) this.battle.getactionspeed(action);` → `sim/battle.ts:2657` `action.speed = action.pokemon.getactionspeed();`, and `switchaction` documents its own fields at `sim/battle-queue.ts:56-69` — `pokemon` is *"the pokemon doing the switch"* (the outgoing body) and `target` is *"pokemon to switch to"*. not covered by #330: #328 says in as many words that `switchin_order.js` governs entry ability order and not which `\|switch\|` lines are emitted. and an instrument gap found while looking, which is why no verdict is filed: this engine already declares an approximation on exactly this axis — `medfails.entryordertie` and `medfails.replaceordertie` (`medicham2-browser.js:1866-1874`), *"showdown shuffles the instaswitch pair; this engine keeps side order and counts the event, because drawing a number here would move the rng stream of every seeded run in the repo"* — and neither counter is published in `data/game-differential.json`, so the artifact cannot tell a declared tie from an ordering defect. what would decide it: publish the two counters in the run, then stage two double-switches with a known speed spread and assert the `\|switch\|` line order extended 2026-08-23 onto the settled artifact: on release `c66976713feb` (961 games, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z, triage `ea26208`) this class is 5, not 3. the two new causes — `ordering :: \|switch\|p1a\|garchomp <> \|switch\|p2b\|blastoise` and `\|switch\|p1a\|swampert <> \|switch\|p2a\|delphox` — are both post-faint replacements, and the second refutes a naive reading from inside the file: the authority moved the slower side first, so replacements do not go in speed order of the incoming body. four of the five carry `max_uses: null` — the mentions are species and species have no `uses` — so a usage-ordered head buries this group while it fires on every double switch and every post-faint replacement. the unpublished-counter ask above is still unmet and is now carried by #375 as well.

open.title: A SIMULTANEOUS DOUBLE WIPE IS A WIN ON THE AUTHORITY AND A DRAW HERE — WINNER-DECIDING, AND INVISIBLE TO EVERY PROTOCOL
open.full: a simultaneous double wipe is a win on the authority and a draw here — winner-deciding, and invisible to every protocol comparison we run. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. the authority, read in the checkout tonight: `sim/battle.ts:2605` — `this.win(faintdata && this.gen > 4 ? faintdata.target.side : null)` inside `checkwin`'s `if (this.sides.every(side => !side.pokemonleft))`, and `faintdata` is the last entry `faintmessages()` shifted off the queue at `:2546`. so in gen 5+ both sides emptying is not a draw: the side whose body fainted last wins — the cartridge rule that the self-destructing player loses, written as a queue position. *(the citation carried in was `:2603`; that is where the `checkwin(` signature sits in this checkout and the `win()` call is two lines below. stated so the next reader does not re-derive it.)* ours has no such rule: `battleresult(s)` in `engine/medicham2-browser.js` (`:24478` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit and the number had already moved to `:24529` by 02:00 — grep the symbol, never this line) compares live-body counts, falls through to total hp fraction, and returns 0.5 for 0-against-0 four lines below — its own header calls that *"dead-even hp tie at the 20-turn horizon"*, which a mutual wipe is not. measured, not argued: `tests/probe_selfdestruct_winner.js` board `w3-simultaneous` — one boom on turn two takes all four remaining bodies — reads showdown `winner="b"` with `pokemonleft p1=0 p2=0` against medicham2's draw. it is declared known-open in that file and reported rather than swept in, and the disagreement is identical clean and under that file's surgical revert, so it is not the self-ko faint position (#331's region) and not the arm. why no instrument we own can see it: every whole-game comparison here compares protocol lines or boards. two engines can emit identical lines to the character and still disagree about who won, so `engine/game_differential.js` has no class for this and never will until a winner is compared. the blast radius is the leaf, not the narration — `battleresult` is what the sealed rollout and the tower end screen read, so every mutual wipe in every rollout is scored half a win, including the ones the authority scores as a loss. will's related case is carried as his hypothesis and not as a fact: perish counters resolve in speed order, so the slowest body faints last and its side would win. #115 landed the speed-ordered residual walk and its own status cell already notes `battle.ts:2604` awards a double ko to the last faint — engine is deriving the perish half now, and nothing in this row asserts it. what would decide the fix: a faint-order field written at every faint site in the engine (`battleresult` cannot acquire the rule without one), then `w3-simultaneous` promoted from reporting to asserting equality against `battle.winner`, with the perish-counter board as the second scenario once engine's derivation lands. instrument owed: a faint-order field written at every faint site in the engine, and `w3-simultaneous` promoted from reporting a known-open verdict to asserting that our result equals the authority’s `battle.winner`.

open.full: the `-boost field 3` class is 9 of the current 96 whole-game divergences and the artifact can name a mechanism for only 2 of them — filed 2026-08-23 by measure with no verdict. read, not re-run, off `data/game-differential.json`: release `59bb68aa89a9`, generated 2026-08-22t22:50:24z, 777 games / 96 diverged / 0 threw, census pin `80e648f34d56`, team pool `b2b61ec40281`. nine causes, each `n=1`, and every one is a magnitude-2 raise on the same slot with a different stat — `\|-boost\|p2a\|atk\|2 <> \|-boost\|p2a\|spe\|2`, `\|-boost\|p1a\|spa\|2 <> \|-boost\|p1a\|atk\|2`, and seven more of that shape. board-material: a +2 on the wrong stat is a different damage roll, a different turn order, or both, for the rest of the game. there is no `-unboost` class in this artifact at all, so the drop half of #351's observation does not appear on this sample. the class name describes the comparator, not the defect, and here that matters: one mechanism is named, seven are unnamed, and the instrument cannot name them. `first_divergences` samples 60 of the 96 games and holds 2 of these 9; in both, our line is `\|-boost\|p2a: scovillain\|spe\|2\|[from] ability: moody`. those two are #351's row and are not re-filed here. the other seven carry no mechanism anywhere in the file — a whole-file scan finds the string `moody` exactly twice, both in those two sampled lines. the reason is structural: `classify()` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:3902` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit — grep the symbol) builds the cause from the normalised line, and the `stat-attribution` entry of `equiv` strips `[from]`/`[of]` from every `-boost` and `-unboost`, 9,631 lines collapsed on this run. that rule is correct for the comparison — a stat line's meaning is (body, stat, direction, amount), and it ships with a red demonstration in both directions — and it is lossy for triage. right instrument, wrong question asked of it. at least two legal mechanisms produce exactly this shape, derived from the format rather than recalled: `moody`, whose legal carriers filtered to the regulation are exactly glalie and scovillain (367 in the abilities column of `data/regulation-usage.json`, clean corpus 17,563 games / 424,933 clicks), and acupressure — `isnonstandard: null`, *"raises a random stat of the user or an ally by 2"*, 42 clicks — which can also raise an ally, a shape moody cannot produce. a third class needs no random draw at all: a deterministic +2 move whose stat we map wrongly. so this class must not be worked as one defect. #351's caveat rides all of it: `game_differential.js` wraps three authority methods to derive a die address (`hitstepaccuracy`, `secondaries`, `getdamage`) and neither a residual ability draw nor a move's own random-stat draw executes in any of them, so whether the two engines even share the draw is not established by this run either. what would decide it: publish the attribution beside the cause — the normaliser can keep stripping it from the comparison while the artifact records what it stripped — and then the seven can be counted before anything is staged. a stat-selection probe means nothing until the class is split. instrument owed: the stripped `[from]` attribution published beside each cause in the artifact, so the nine can be split by mechanism before anything is staged. extended 2026-08-23 onto the settled artifact — the headline count above is not rewritten, it is superseded by a different sample. on release `c66976713feb` (961 games / 95 diverged / 0 threw, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z, triage `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-remaining-56.md`, `ea26208`) the `-boost field 3` class is 6, not 9, in five causes (one with `n=2`); the `-unboost` half this row recorded as absent is back as exactly one cause (`\|-unboost\|p1a\|spa\|1 <> \|-unboost\|p1a\|spe\|1`, moody's drop shape, which is #351's original observation); attribution recoverable from the file is 1 of the 6 and no more — a whole-file scan finds `moody` once and `acupressure` zero times; and the candidate split is now bounded from the pinned pool rather than argued — in `data/team-pool-frozen`, `acupressure` appears in one line each of `games.bo3.jsonl` and `games.ots.jsonl` (the same set) against `moody` at 813 + 204, so acupressure can explain at most 1 of the 6, open.title: THE 22 DAMAGING `self` MOVES FAIL THROUGH A DOOR THAT HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED, AND THE DECLARATION LIVED ONLY IN A CHANG
open.full: the 22 damaging `self` moves fail through a door that has never been measured, and the declaration lived only in a changelog — filed 2026-08-23 by measure, no verdict. #343 staged the one heal-primary status member (a failed roost, where we emit the `-fail` and then also the `-singleturn` and ground a body the authority leaves flying) and that pass declared the rest open rather than sweeping them in — correct, the scope of a fix is the scope that was probed. but the declaration existed only in changelog 5.74.0 and in no register row, which is the same failure as a figure that lives only in prose: nothing could print it, so nothing could act on it. membership derived from the format tonight, filtered to the regulation, not typed: 25 legal moves carry a `self` effect; 3 are status — baton pass, roost, shed tail — and exactly one of those is heal-primary (roost, `self.heal` true); 22 are damaging. ten carry `self.boosts` (close combat, superpower, hammer arm, ice hammer, headlong rush, draco meteor, leaf storm, overheat, make it rain, armor cannon), eleven `self.volatilestatus` (hyper beam, giga impact, outrage, thrash, petal dance, raging fury, uproar, blast burn, hydro cannon, frenzy plant, rock wrecker), one `self.onhit` (burn up). this is not a tail: 32,135 clicks of 424,933 in the clean corpus — 7.6% — and close combat alone is 18,600, with draco meteor 3,291, make it rain 2,811, overheat 1,879 and hyper beam 1,708. the door is the one #343 found: `runmoveeffects` writes `damage[i] = false` on a refused hit, `spreadmovehit` sets `targets[i] = false`, and step 4 `selfdrops` skips a false target — so for each of the 22 the open question is whether our self-rider fires on a hit the authority refused (a protect, a type immunity, a miss, a substitute). for the ten boost members that is a stat stage that does or does not exist; for the eleven volatile members it is whether the user is locked or recharging, which decides the whole of the following turn. nothing here claims they are wrong. the failure path has not been measured on any of the 22, on either engine, and no `defect` token is filed — an unprobed member is not a defect, and calling it one would corrupt the open-defect clause exactly as much as missing a real one. what would decide it: one staged pair per `self` shape rather than per move — close combat into a protect asserting the defence drop on both engines or on neither; hyper beam into a ghost asserting `mustrecharge` on both or on neither, which is the board #161 records wire 43 getting backwards once already; burn up into a target that refuses it for the `onhit` shape. three probes cover 22 members, and the shapes are derived, not listed. instrument owed: one staged pair per `self` shape — boosts, volatilestatus, onhit — asserting the self-rider fires on both engines or on neither when the authority refused the hit.

open.title: THE DIFFERENTIAL MIRRORS A FORCED SWITCH BY SPECIES NAME, SO IT CANNOT EXPRESS A RENAMED BODY OR ONE ALREADY ON THE FIEL
open.full: the differential mirrors a forced switch by species name, so it cannot express a renamed body or one already on the field — one instrument defect wearing three faces. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. `mirrorforcedswitch` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:3743` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit and had moved to `:3754` by 02:00 — grep the symbol, and it is exported) turns medicham2's replacement into a showdown choice with `roster.findindex((q, n) => !claimed.has(n) && !q.isactive && !q.fainted && id(q.species.id) === id(body.name))`. a miss writes `cannot`, which becomes `mirrorimpossible` and then, at the call site, `endreason = "the boards parted — medicham2's placement cannot be expressed to showdown"` at `:3533`. the message already distinguishes the two ways to miss: *"does not have under that name"* — the body was renamed (transform, forme change) — and *"has but cannot switch in (fainted/active)"* — the body is already on the field. neither is expressible by a name-keyed lookup, and both are the instrument, not the engine. measured on the current artifact (`data/game-differential.json`, release `59bb68aa89a9`, 777 games, 2026-08-22t22:50:24z): `declared_gaps.forced_switch_unmirrorable` = 11, against 959 slots mirrored and 7 legitimately passed, first instance *"p1: slot 1 holds froslass, which showdown has but cannot switch in (fainted/active)"*. the middle arm ends 2 of 777 games on it, `top-tie-first` 2 and `bottom-tie-first` 5 — and one of those end reasons names `froslassmega`, the renamed face sitting in the published record. every game that ends this way is a game whose remaining turns were never compared. three staged scenarios are this one mechanism and were proved to be, not assumed: `imposter-copies-the-body-opposite`, `hungerswitch-flips-every-turn` and `roar-drags-whoever-is-standing-there` in `tests/staged_board.js` return the identical short verdict at the identical turn with the identical `endreason` under all four arms, with `err=null`, `statediv=null` and the engines agreeing on every board, byte-identical on releases `18b227eee69f` and `39631097fcc7`. not the arm, not the dice, not the engine. and nothing gates them: `tests/staged_board.js` is not `test-*.js` so `tests/run-all.js` does not discover it, while seven `test-*.js` files require it as a library — `test-assert-mode`, `test-forme-assert`, `test-middle-stall-address`, `test-perish-song`, `test-roster-arm-pin`, `test-switch-back-renamed`, `test-volatile-duration` — and `tests/test-forced-switch-mirror.js` drives the exported helper directly. one fix, nine instruments. #346 is closed and is not this row: it fixed the fallback's lack of memory of what the other slot had just taken on a double ko. this is the key itself, and #346 must not be read as covering it. what would decide it: mirror on the roster index medicham2 chose rather than on a name, then stage a transform and a forme change through a forced switch and assert the game does not stop. sources `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-wrong-arm-callers.md` and `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-drag-and-fail.md`. instrument owed: a clause that fails while `declared_gaps.forced_switch_unmirrorable` is non-zero, plus a staged transform and a staged forme change driven through a forced switch.

open.title: `tests/test-precharge-order.js` PUBLISHED "83 CHECKS" MEASURED ON AN ARM IT NEVER NAMED, AND 21 OTHER CALLERS ARE IN THE
open.full: `tests/test-precharge-order.js` published "83 checks" measured on an arm it never named, and 21 other callers are in the same state with 7 already cleared — filed 2026-08-23 by measure. `primary_arm` on the live driver is `middle` (read off it, not assumed), so a caller that omits `arm` silently gets live dice. `test-precharge-order.js` was screened under three arms and it moves: under `bottom-tie-first` four of its arms produce more protocol — 11→12, 14→16, 12→13, 10→11 lines — because secondaries fire and crits land that the middle arm did not draw. its verdict does not flip today, because both engines share the arm and agree either way; what is weaker is the claim. *"the two protocol streams do not part"* means less on a board where fewer things happened, and `docs/engine.md:1596` and `:1650` publish "five arms, 83 checks" measured exactly there. the population is 22, not the 27 first reported, derived by parsing each `playgame` call site's balanced argument list instead of grepping for the string `arm:`: three files pass the arm as an es6 shorthand (`{ script, arm }`, no colon) and were accused wrongly, and two never call the driver's `playgame` at all — `replaygame` contains it as a substring. and it is bigger in the other direction: 4 more reach it indirectly through `tests/staged_board.js`'s exported `runone(sc, patchedsrc)`, which takes no arm parameter at all, and 7 more are the driver's own self-proofs — `planted_divergence_proof`, `directed` and `knock_off_roadmap_80` are published blocks of `data/game-differential.json` riding them, and a plant that has to beat live dice is a weaker red than one on a corner. 14 of the 22 publish a figure; 8 were screened and 7 are byte-identical across `middle`, `top-tie-first` and `bottom-tie-first` — inert with evidence, which is the noise floor the one positive rests on. will's rule governs the repair — fix one at a time, re-measure, withdraw only what moves. seven figures have already been cleared rather than withdrawn on suspicion, which is the point of screening before retracting. a correction is owed to `docs/engine.md`, which publishes 27 in two places; engine owns that ledger. this row does not withdraw the 83. it has not been re-measured on a named arm, so what is established is that the instrument is arm-dependent — not what the number becomes. source `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-wrong-arm-callers.md`. instrument owed: a check that every `playgame` call site names an arm, so an unpinned caller fails by name instead of being audited by hand once a quarter.

open.title: THE 5.74.0 RETRACTION'S MECHANISM IS NOT SUPPORTED BY EITHER ARTIFACT: THE TEAM-STORE FIELD HAS EXISTED SINCE 2026-08-07
open.full: the 5.74.0 retraction's mechanism is not supported by either artifact: the team-store field has existed since 2026-08-07 and both runs declare the same frozen pool. filed 2026-08-23 by measure, with no verdict on the remainder. changelog 5.74.0 revised its divergence-rate-over-usable from 9.7% to 11.69% and gave two reasons: that `--team-store data\team-pool-frozen` *"did not take"*, and that "`data/game-differential.json` records no team-store field at all". the second is false. `steer_stamp.team_store_pinned_to = team_store \|\| null` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:4849` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; the file is under active engine edit — grep the symbol) writes it unconditionally in the swarm block, under its own comment *"said out loud either way … an unpinned run that looks like a pinned one is the whole problem"*, and `git log -s` puts it in `b168490`, 2026-08-07 16:34 — fifteen days before the entry saying it does not exist. and the first is contradicted by the record. read out of git rather than re-run: the earlier artifact (`b26c2d4`, generated 2026-08-22t21:17:11z, 961 games / 95 diverged) carries `steering.team_store_pinned_to = "data\\\\team-pool-frozen"` and `steering.team_pool_teams = 8778`; the corrected one (`head`, 22:50:24z, 777 / 96) carries `"data/team-pool-frozen"` and the same 8778. `team_store` is the sole input to `swarm.buildswarm(..., { storedir })`, and `data/team-pool-frozen/` is a 2026-08-12 snapshot whose `games.bo3.jsonl` is 109,006,606 bytes against the live store's 167,972,026 — a live pool cannot yield the frozen pool's team count, so both runs read the frozen pool. what actually differs is `team_pool_picked` (1,968 against 1,597) and therefore `team_pool_digest` (`0d103fb9fa87` against `b2b61ec40281`), and `buildswarm` is asked for `max(games * 2, 18)` teams — i.e. the two runs requested different sample sizes. and the requested count is recoverable from the record, though neither artifact stores it. there is no `games_requested`, no argv and no flag block in either file — the same gap this row is about, one level up. but `buildswarm` computes `per = max(1, floor(max(games * 2, 18) / cfg.length))`, both runs carry 9 configs, and both publish `picked` per config: seven of the nine sit exactly on the cap, at 266 for `b26c2d4` and 213 for `head`. inverting that puts `--games` in [1197, 1201] for the earlier run and [959, 962] for the later one — so the two runs asked for materially different sizes, roughly 1200 against roughly 960, and 1200 and 960 are the only round numbers in those intervals. `coverage_stop` is `null` in both and the source says that field is *"null on a fixed-count run"*, so both took an explicit count and neither was `--until-covered`. the driver clamps, and it clamps per config rather than to the whole pool — the picker is `for (i = 0; i < matching.length && picked.length < per; i += step)`, and the record shows `omit-protect` at 99/99 and `omit-priority` at 7/7 in both runs. identical starvation is a third independent sign that the two read the same pool. so neither run got the count it asked for: about 1200 requested against 961 played (80.1%), and about 960 against 777 (80.9%). the shortfall is per-config starvation inside the frozen pool, present in both runs and in the same proportion — it is not a live store. what remains unknown and is not guessed: which exact integer was passed, and why the second run asked for the smaller one. nothing in the record carries a command line, and nothing was re-run to find out. neither figure is withdrawn by this row and neither may be entered in a retraction registry on its account: 11.69% is a rate on 777 games and 9.7% is a rate on 961, both on the frozen pool — two samples, not a pinned one and an unpinned one. what this row disputes is the cause that was published beside them, and nothing else. the real defect is that nothing reads the field. the only reader of `team_store_pinned_to` anywhere under `engine/` or `tests/` is `engine/replay_one.js:240`, and it reads the dump artifact rather than this one; no gate, no provenance clause and no `status.js` line compares a published claim's asserted pool against the artifact's declared pool or its `team_pool_digest`. a receipt nobody presents is not a receipt — which is the true form of what 5.74.0 was reaching for, and it is why a wrong pin would still be invisible today. #288 is the general row (a corpus snapshot id beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file) and stays open; this is the specific case where the id already exists and is unread. what would decide it: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact does not declare, plus one re-measure of the 961/777 gap at a single requested game count. instrument owed: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact’s own `steering.team_store_pinned_to` and `team_pool_digest` do not declare.

open.title: THE DERIVED RETRACTION REGISTRY MATCHES ON A ROUNDED VALUE, SO ONE RETRACTED FIGURE ACCUSED 52 DOCUMENT LINES THAT SAY A
open.full: the derived retraction registry matches on a rounded value, so one retracted figure accused 52 document lines that say a different number — measured 2026-08-23 by measure, and it is live at baseline today. `retractionviolations` in `engine/docs_scan.js` accepts a hit when `number(e.value.tofixed(f.dp)) === f.value`. that tolerance was built for a real case — a document writing `63%` for a retracted `63.2%` is restating it — and it has no bound, so `(9.7).tofixed(0)` is `"10"` and a retracted `9.7%` matches every bare `10%` in the repository. measured: when one register row caused `9.7%` to enter the registry, that single entry produced 56 violations, of which 52 were a bare `10%` — a 93% false-positive rate on one entry, across `docs/engine.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/literature-v2.md`, `docs/miltank.md`, `docs/abra-whitepaper.md` and `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md`, hitting *"flare blitz's 10% burn"*, *"top 10% in singles"*, *"the 0-10% or 90-100% bin"* and *"~10% of its useful size"*. this is not about that one figure and it is not new — it is firing at baseline right now. with that entry removed the clause sits exactly at its baseline of 10 keys, and 12 of the 17 surviving raw violations are rounding collisions rather than exact matches: `docs/backlog.md:215` *"we produce the single most common set 48% of the time"* and `docs/archive/session-2026-08-02.md:113` *"sucker punch's 48% failure prices the missing opponent model"* are both accused of restating the retracted mirror figure 47.5%, and neither is about it. a second, independent half: `isdistinctive` admits any percent. it is `f => f.pct \|\| f.value >= 1000`, so a two-significant-figure percentage qualifies — and `docs/engine.md` carries the literal cell `\| into a bright powder holder (100 x 0.9 = 90) \| 10.3% \| 9.7% \|`, an accuracy, which any retracted `9.7%` rate would accuse forever. the registry's own header already makes this exact argument and then exempts percents from it: it records that a bare `17` once flagged ninety lines and concludes *"a registry that fires on every occurrence of a small integer is worse than no registry, because it is the thing people switch off."* a percent with two significant figures is a small integer wearing a unit. and the sharpest half: the extractor cannot tell a figure that is retracted from a figure named in a sentence about a retraction. rule 2 registers `<determiner> <number>` on any line containing `retract`, so a row whose finding is that a figure was not withdrawn is read as withdrawing it. that is what happened here: #367 states in terms that neither of its two rates is withdrawn, and the derivation entered one of them as retracted anyway. the row was reworded so it can only be read one way — which fixed the symptom and not this — and the baseline was deliberately not touched, because adding entries to `data/docs-currency-baseline.json` to quiet a false positive is the laundering that file's own rule forbids. this is #148 in a clause that is genuinely valuable when it fires correctly, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than loosening: the same derivation is what caught the deck's `63.2%` restated as fact after the white paper withdrew it in writing, and an over-firing gate is the one people learn to ignore. what would decide the fix is three cases and not a preferred implementation, because the shape decision is the open part: a retracted `63.2%` must still match a document writing `63%`; a retracted `9.7%` must not match a bare `10%`; a retracted `47.5%` must not match a sucker punch `48%` failure rate. the current rule satisfies only the first. instrument owed: a red demonstration pair per matching rule in `engine/docs_scan.js` on synthetic documents, in the style of the `equal`/`distinct` pairs the differential's own normaliser already carries, plus a distinctiveness floor for percents stated as a rule rather than as a magnitude status cell of 2026-08-23, moved here verbatim 2026-09-11 by measure, so the open status cell can say the over-fire is fixed without its own history counting it as broken: open — instrument defect in `engine/docs_scan.js` (measure owns it); over-fire measured at 52 of 56 on one entry and 12 of 17 at baseline, no figure withdrawn and no baseline entry added to quiet it (filed 2026-08-23)

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE ONE TOOL BUILT TO PRINT WHAT THE REGISTER CANNOT SEE ABOUT ITSELF IS FED BY A SINGLE ARTIFACT THAT IS 11.4 DAYS OLD,
open.full: the one tool built to print what the register cannot see about itself is fed by a single artifact that is 11.4 days old, so it prints `unregistered: 0` and that zero carries no information — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `engine/open_work.js`’s whole justification is that *a register cannot audit itself*, and its unregistered half is the stronger of its two signals because it is measured rather than filed. run 2026-08-23: `measured_disagreements: 0, unregistered: 0`. the reason is in its own output — the only instrument it reads is `data/interaction-matrix.json`, generated 2026-08-11t22:00:06z, and it prints the warning itself: *"11.4 days old. anything read out of it describes the engine of that day, not this one."* it is doing exactly what it was built to do and the answer is still empty, which is worse than a red: a zero from a blind instrument reads identically to a zero from a clear one. measured against it the same day, the reports in `docs/_reports/` filed nine defects with no register row on 2026-08-22 and at least four more on 2026-08-23 (#377, #378, #382, #383 among them), every one of which unregistered reported as zero. the fix is not to regenerate the matrix — that makes one number current and leaves the tool reading one instrument. it is that unregistered must read the artifacts that actually measure this engine today: `data/game-differential.json`’s causes, the three `data/roster.*.json` stages, and `data/all-mechanics-fire.json`, each matched against the register by subject and each stamped with its own age. instrument owed: those four sources wired into `open_work.js`’s measured half, and a refusal — not a zero — when every source it reads is older than the engine

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE WHOLE-GAME HEADLINE SILENTLY CHANGED QUANTITY IN AUGUST AND NOTHING LABELS WHICH ONE IT IS, SO THE REGISTER’S OWN TR
open.full: the whole-game headline silently changed quantity in august and nothing labels which one it is, so the register’s own trend line compares two different measurements — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `wholegameclause` published a raw rate (`diverged / games`) until the declared-divergence exemption landed 2026-08-18, and has published an undeclared rate (`(diverged - declared - decision_cleared) / games`) since. both are correct and neither is named in the sentence it prints: the string is `<n> of <games> = <pct>% diverge`, with the raw figure appearing only inside a parenthetical and only when something was subtracted. #218 therefore carries 39.6% (raw, 2026-08-12), 69.9% (undeclared, 2026-08-18) and 8.0% (undeclared, 2026-08-23) in one cell as if they were one series, and the raw-to-raw pair — 39.6% against 8.5% — has to be reconstructed by hand from a field the sentence does not print. and the artifact offers three more numbers the headline is not. the same run carries `arms[].diverged` at middle 82, top-tie-first 68 and bottom-tie-first 77 of 961; the headline reads 77 because 82 minus 5 declared is 77. a coordinator read that collision as the gate quoting a corner by omission and ordered a correction and a defect row on the strength of it. refuted by driving the shipping function on perturbed copies of the artifact: the headline is invariant to both arm figures and moves only with the top-level `diverged` and with the declared set (#218). no arm-selection defect exists and this row is not one — it is registered because the near-miss cost a correction cycle, and because the same collision will recur every time raw minus declared lands on one of the other two arms. what would fix it: the clause names its quantity in the sentence (`undeclared`), prints the raw rate beside it unconditionally rather than only when something was subtracted, and prints the arm it describes by id; and the artifact carries the published headline as its own field so a reader never has to reconstruct which of five numbers the gate meant. instrument owed: an assertion that the published headline string names its quantity and its arm, in the style of the composition-vs-headline check #292 already added to this clause

open.title: THE DAMAGE DIFFERENTIAL'S REFERENCE ENTERS AT `moveHit` AND NEVER RUNS `ModifyMove`, SO FIVE MEGA ABILITIES ARE INVISIBL

the next line and this does not … recorded as owed rather than smuggled in here"*). the authority runs both — `sim/battle-actions.ts:431` and `:439` — while the harness enters 931 lines lower at `movehit` (`:1370`). mega sol is the same hole through a different door: `pokemon#effectiveweather` (`sim/pokemon.ts:2198`) requires `battle.activepokemon`, which only `runmove` sets. every row is proven, not inferred: for each, showdown's published number equals medicham's own number with the attacker's ability cleared to `none`, to the unit, at both corners — `cameruptmega flashcannon -> gengar` 69-82 (ours 90-106, x1.30 sheer force), `kangaskhanmega fakeout -> pinsir` 37-45 (ours 44-55, the bonded packet), `gyaradosmega earthquake -> rotomwash` 0-0 (ours 136-160, levitate broken by mold breaker), `meganiummega weatherball -> lycanrocmidnight` 21-25 (ours 64-75, the private sun), `lopunnymega fakeout -> gourgeistsuper` 0-0 (ours 33-40, scrappy). knob-cleared both ways. current count, read off the artifact generated 2026-08-23t09:07:44z: of the 40 published rows, sheer force / camerupt 11, parental bond / kangaskhan 7, mold breaker / gyarados 3, mega sol / meganium 2, scrappy / lopunny 1 = 24, and after #392 these plus castform are the whole residual. fur coat is not a defect despite looking like one — measured at x2 defence, and `furfrou` diverges only because medicham correctly lets mold breaker through it and the reference cannot. this is on the critical path for lifting quarantine even though it is the ruler: `engine/quarantine.js:599` requires `disagreed === 0`, and an instrument defect holds that clause shut exactly as an engine defect does. how many more rows of this class exist, derived: of the 76 legal megas, 11 carry a slot-0 ability with an `onmodifymove` / `onpreparehit` / `onmodifypriority` handler; across all legal abilities there are 22 such carriers. a related structural blindness, stated so it is not mistaken for agreement: the harness never runs `onpreparehit` either, so protean rows agree for the wrong reason — a green row that asks nothing. instrument owed: run `modifymove` in the harness (or exclude these carriers from the comparison and say so in the artifact), then re-measure at seed 20260804

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A CASTFORM-SNOWY BODY IS NEVER RECONCILED TO AN EMPTY SKY, AND WHETHER THAT IS THE HARNESS OR THE ENGINE RESTS ON A READ
open.full: a castform-snowy body is never reconciled to an empty sky, and whether that is the harness or the engine rests on a read of the source rather than on an execution — 16 of the 41 remaining damage divergences, 39% of the residual, filed 2026-08-23 by measure with no verdict. `mc_key.js` now admits battle-only formes, so the pool contains `palafinhero`, `aegislashblade`, `mimikyubusted`, `morpekohangry` and `castformsnowy`; the three with no switch-in precondition produced zero rows across 116 draws, and the two carrying one produced all 31 (the other is #392). proof by control, 16/16: rebuilding the body as base `castform` reproduces showdown's number to the unit on every published row, and base stats are identical across all four castform rows in `mc.mons`, so a types-only revert is numerically complete. the reading that makes it the instrument: medicham does model this — `syncweatherformes` finds no matching sky and falls to `revertstotypes: ['normal']`, reached through `syncfieldtypes`, which is called at battle init (`medicham2-browser.js:14522`) — while the harness builds bodies and calls `dmgrange` directly and never calls it, and the showdown side really switches in so forecast's `onstart` fires. `applyentryeffects` does not revert it (measured: types stay `["ice"]`), so only the init-level call would. the probe that settles it, and it belongs to whoever holds the engine: build a lead pair with `castform-snowy`, run one `battle()` init, assert the body's types read `["normal"]` on turn 1 with no weather, control being the same body under snow reading `["ice"]`. if it reads `["ice"]`, this is a second engine defect of #392's shape and outranks #393. and a stale load-bearing comment: `medicham2-browser.js:12946-12948` still says `data/engine-data.js` holds no row for castform-sunny/rainy/snowy — that is the whole stated reason forecast is modelled as a retype with the species label deliberately wrong — and #204 landed those five rows on 2026-08-22; `mc.mons` holds all four today. the blocker named in the comment is gone and the premise should stop being cited. which scoreboard, declared before the run: castform is 0.08% of teams (28 of 36,696), so expect the pinned pool not to move — 39% of the published damage residual for 0.08% of the metagame. instrument owed: the init probe above

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE DAMAGE DIFFERENTIAL PUBLISHES 40 ROWS OF HOWEVER MANY IT FOUND, SO A TAIL OF 16 HAD TO BE RECONSTRUCTED BY HAND BEFO
open.full: the damage differential publishes 40 rows of however many it found, so a tail of 16 had to be reconstructed by hand before anyone could group it — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `tests/test-engine-diff.js:954` writes `worst: bad.slice(0, 40)` over a list sorted by move usage descending, and every `arms` list is capped at 40 the same way (`:975`) — the union of all sixteen arm lists is the same 40 triples as the midpoint's, so the arms do not recover the tail either. at `disagreed: 56` that hid 16 rows, all with move `uses` <= 1507, and recovering them required replaying the harness's lcg (seed 20260804, whose only in-loop consumer is `pick`) and re-deriving each family by the harness's own rules — a reconstruction that reproduced 39 of the 40 published rows and is therefore near-exact rather than exact. the cost was not academic: the hidden 16 contained 8 of the 15 mimikyu-busted rows (#392) and 6 of the 11 sheer force rows, so the artifact under-reported the engine defect's size by more than half. today's re-run (`disagreed: 41`) hides only 1, so the cap is currently almost harmless — which is exactly when it is cheapest to raise. what would fix it: raise or remove the cap, or publish a family tally beside the truncated list so the count is readable without a replay. individual rows can already be confirmed one at a time with `--case att,move,def` (`:762`), and the run is deterministic, so nothing is lost — only hidden. instrument owed: the cap raised, or a per-family count written into the artifact

the primary arm is 82 of 961 = 8.5%, or 8.34% over the 959 usable once the 2 mid-void games are removed, which is the only rate the artifact itself computes (see #387 for why the quantity is unlabelled). this row groups the middle arm's 82, because `classes[].causes[]` is the middle arm's table and nothing else in the artifact is broken out per arm at cause level. the single most important fact here: `state_mode: false`, `end_state_mode: false`, `state: null`, `end_state: null` — this was a protocol run, no board was compared at any turn boundary and no end board was compared, so by will's standing rule (*a divergence is narration-only when something measured it as narration-only*) the board-material split cannot be read off it at all, and `data/state-ladder.json` may not be substituted (16 days old, no `engine_release`, and it predates the artifact's own declared `baseline_reset`). until `node engine/game_differential.js --games 961 --end-state --release c36782953dee --team-store data/team-pool-frozen --write` runs, "board-material zero" has no denominator — and even a clean end-state run does not clear the `-fail` family, which needs `engine/move_result_state.js` (#382) because `board_state.js` compares no move-result field. coverage, honestly: 82 of 82 attributed at cause-string level; open.title: SIX SWITCH-IN / ON-HIT EFFECTS DO NOT FIRE AT ALL IN A REAL GAME, EVERY ONE BOARD-MATERIAL BY STRUCTURE, AND EVERY ONE A
open.full: six switch-in / on-hit effects do not fire at all in a real game, every one board-material by structure, and every one already carrying a populated tag row — 7 of the whole-game 82, filed 2026-08-23 by measure. read off `data/game-differential.json` (release `c36782953dee`, 2026-08-23t06:10:58z); none of the six has a champions override, so the mainline handler is the authority. forecast (2 games, 15 uses): the authority writes `-formechange … castform-rainy \|[msg]\|[from] ability: forecast` in rain and the forme carries a different type — board-material without argument; the tag `formefollowsweather` already holds the full `byweather` / `typesbyweather` map, and #204 landed the missing bodies (see also #394). regenerator (1 game, 1,855 uses — the highest here): `-heal … 170/170 \|[from] ability: regenerator\|[silent]` on switch-out; `[silent]` but hp-bearing, which is exactly why a blanket "`[silent]` is narration" normalisation rule must never be written. psychic terrain (1 game): the authority blocks a prankster-boosted thunder wave into a grounded annihilape and we let the paralysis land — a status that should not exist. symbiosis (1, 69 uses): neither the `-activate` nor the item transfer happens; (b) still open — the locked phantom force that announces and deals nothing on its second turn. untouched by the above, never staged, no instrument. instrument owed: a two-turn phantom force asserting damage on turn 2, control being the same pair with the lock broken

open.title: TWO PUBLISHED SEED-PREVALENCE FIGURES ARE WITHHELD — THE GENERATOR'S SPECIES LOOKUP DROPPED EVERY FORME — 2026-08-23, ME
open.full: two published seed-prevalence figures are withheld — the generator's species lookup dropped every forme — 2026-08-23, measure. `engine/rollout_seed_prevalence.js:95` read `mc.mons[base(sp)]`, and `base()` ends in `norm()`, which strips the hyphen `mc.mons` keys every forme with. so `rotom-wash` asked the table for `rotomwash`, got nothing, and was handed an empty dataset moveset — which the caller compares against the sheet's declared four and scores as *"the moves differ"*. a miss can only push `movesdiffer` up, so the bias is one-directional. measured over `data/games.bo3.jsonl`: 47 of 256 store species names, 10,980 of 144,260 brought bodies (7.61%); at the sheet-body level 19,236 of 231,924 bodies hit it and 7,177 (3.095% of all bodies) flip true → false once the row is found — top flippers floette-eternal 3,022, arcanine-hisui 1,919, lycanroc-dusk 1,059. withheld, not annotated (claude.md: *"a caption is not a quarantine"*), from `docs/search.md` r14 (the section headline, the one-line verdict, the prevalence table's `#248 moveset` and `any` rows, and the two r14 cells in the argmax-paired reach column), from `docs/miltank.md` §3.9, from this row's #248 closure text, and from `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md`: `pct_248_bench_moves_differ` and `pct_any` of `data/rollout-seed-prevalence.json`. scope is bounded and measured, not assumed: `datasetmoves` is called at exactly one site in the generator and feeds only `movesdiffer`; `pct_any` is an or containing it. the other four rates — `17.655`, `17.053`, `13.089`, `0.061` — are computed independently and stand. no corrected value is estimated: the direction is known, the magnitude is not, and a body-level flip rate does not translate one-for-one to a decision point that ors over the whole live bench. the four rows closed on this batch (#247, #248, #249, #250) do not rest on the withheld figure and are not reopened — each closed on `tests/test-rollout-seed.js` shown red first with its own control, the prevalence figures were published as ceilings on reach beside them (`docs/search.md`: *"a ceiling on reach, not a count of flipped argmaxes"*), and the actual effect was measured separately and independently at 61/131 paired argmax flips under common random numbers (#278). #247's and #249's quoted shares are among the four unaffected. restored by a pinned re-run, not an unpinned one: `head -n 14102 data/games.bo3.jsonl > data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl && node engine/rollout_seed_prevalence.js --store data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl`. the store has grown 14,102 → 19,401 games since 2026-08-14, so an unpinned run is a different question; a correct pin must return `decisionpoints: 190378` exactly, which the bug cannot have touched. the lookup itself is already fixed and goes through `engine/mc_key.js` — verified by: `node tests/test-mc-key.js` scope narrowed 2026-08-24 by measure — the `verified by` on this row does not decide its open half, and the register was overstating because of it. `engine/register_reality.js` ran `node tests/test-mc-key.js`, read exit 0, and filed this row as the only stale row in the file — an open row whose instrument is green. that is correct and it is not evidence the row should close: the marker decides the lookup fix, which is landed and gated, and it is structurally incapable of deciding the withheld figures, which are restored only by the pinned re-run this row already specifies (`head -n 14102 data/games.bo3.jsonl > data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl`, and a correct pin must return `decisionpoints: 190378` exactly). the two figures remain withheld, not annotated, and the re-run has not been done. instrument owed for the open half: nothing in the repository fails while those two figures are absent

open.full: a rollout has no coin to flip on an entry tie, so it takes one branch deterministically — filed 2026-08-24 by engine, and it is loud rather than silent. the entry tie is now decided by the shared `tie` die exactly as the move queue’s is. but a caller that hands `battleinit` no rng — every rollout, every census probe, miltank’s search — has no die, so the tied group keeps the order the selection sort handed it. `medfails.entryordertienodie` counts every occurrence, which is why this is a row rather than a hole. it is not a correctness defect against the authority: the differential pins the die to a constant on both sides anyway, so the measured whole-game number does not move either way. it is a search-quality question. decision needed from will, and it is card 4 of `docs/_reports/2026-08-24-ordering-cards.md`: leave rollouts deterministic on a tie (cheap, reproducible, biased to one branch), or give `battleinit` a die and accept that every existing seeded baseline in the repository shifts will ruled 2026-08-24, and the ruling splits the row in two. no die for rollouts — but a rollout must recognise that a tie is a tie and plan both branches rather than silently taking one and calling it the future. that is two pieces of work with two owners. the engine half is live: make the tie visible where it resolves, so a caller can see that the order it received was one branch of a coin rather than a fact. the search half is paused and is filed only, not queued — miltank is not being invested in while medicham is being corrected, so "plan both branches" is recorded here so it is not lost, and no work is scheduled against it. the cost the row named does not arise: no existing seeded baseline shifts, because no die is being added.

open.full: a single-game replay is not reproducible in isolation, so every isolated debugging session in this repo is quietly unreliable — found 2026-08-24 by engine, filed by measure. replaying one diverging pair on its own gives a different game from the same pair played in sequence inside the 961-game run, and the difference is not small: it changes which turn the game diverges on, and sometimes whether it diverges at all. measured twice inside one batch — the phazing game diverged at turn 3 as the 11th game in a process and at turn 1 played alone, on a mega-order speed tie between two identical aerodactyls; the redirect game diverged at turn 11 in sequence and at turn 10 on a different cause alone. the cause is named: the tie key and the mid-battle address log are process-scoped in a way the per-game reset does not fully clear, so a game's dice depend on how many games ran before it. it was shown not to be any one batch's doing — reproduced with `engine/medicham2-browser.js` reverted to head in the same isolated position. the consequence is the part that matters: a single-game replay is a fine way to read a divergence and a bad way to prove one was fixed; only the full run played in the same order on both arms is an attribution. nothing published has been shown wrong because of it — the standing figures all come from the sequenced run — but every `replay_one.js` session is affected. what would decide it: play one pair alone and at position n of a run with both engines' per-game reset instrumented and assert the first divergence is identical; then reset the tie key and the address log per game and assert it again. instrument owed

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `tests/test-resolution-order.js` DIES OOM AT NODE'S DEFAULT HEAP, AND HAS BEEN RED FOR LONGER THAN ANY ONE BATCH — FOUND
open.full: `tests/test-resolution-order.js` dies oom at node's default heap, and has been red for longer than any one batch — found 2026-08-26 by engine. the file exits 134 with `fatal error: reached heap limit allocation failed` after printing ~17 `release store overridden` lines. it is not this batch's, proved rather than argued: `git show head:engine/medicham2-browser.js` was put in place and the file re-run — same exit 134, same message — and it also ooms with the batch's own behaviour knob switched off. the engine is fine: at `--max-old-space-size=6144` it passes, 26 arms staged, 1 known-open (the declared multi-hit granularity arm), 0 failing. the cause is named and not fixed: the file opens a release per arm and each snapshot loads the frozen engine plus its lazily-read data files, so ~26 of them are resident at once. why it matters beyond the red: every gate in this repo is read as an exit code, `tests/run-all.js` spawns children without a heap flag, and an instrument that dies on memory is indistinguishable at the exit code from an instrument that found a defect — which is this project's signature failure wearing the other hat. what would decide it: open one release for the whole file (the arms already share an id) or release each snapshot after its arm, then re-run at the default heap and assert exit 0 with the same 26/1/0 line. the runner half is closed 2026-08-27 by measure and the leak is not, and the two are deliberately not merged. this row named two defects in one paragraph: a per-arm snapshot leak in the check, and *"`tests/run-all.js` spawns children without a heap flag, and an instrument that dies on memory is indistinguishable at the exit code from an instrument that found a defect"*. the second is the runner's and is fixed: a check declares `abra-heap: <mb>` in its own header, `plan()` derives it and passes `--max-old-space-size` before the script path, and `--list` prints the honoured value so the derivation can be seen to have fired. it is derived from the child rather than tabled in the runner for the reason the ci job list was replaced — a table of costs goes stale and the staleness surfaces as exit 134 on a machine nobody is watching. and an oom still fails: it is annotated `out of heap`, never downgraded to a skip, because a crash filed as "did not run" is the same laundering as a crash filed as a verdict. verified by capturing the real argv of all 165 children with `spawnsync` stubbed — exactly one carries the flag — and by measuring that the flag moves the ceiling 2,240 mb → 6,336 mb in that position and does nothing at all after the script path. the leak is untouched and this row stays open on it: nothing was done to the 26 resident snapshots, and measure did not re-run the file (it plays games and engine held the play layer), so the 26/1/0 line is engine's measurement of 2026-08-26 and not a fresh one. instrument owed
