open.full: `new battle()` validates nothing — a probe could measure a mechanic this format does not contain. will: *"why dont we use showdowns teams validator that is universal truth"*. now it does. `engine/champions_sim.checklegal` asks the `teamvalidator` — the authority adr-002 names, through the instance `packteam` already builds — and splits its complaints into banned (the format does not contain this; always fatal) and pairing (this species cannot hold this; a legitimate isolation, declarable in writing). it catches strictly more than an `isnonstandard` check: *"meganium can't learn flamethrower"* is a legal move on a species that cannot have it, and that set was hand-staged on 2026-08-08. caught two defects in its own harness on the first run — `tackle` is `past` and every inert slot carried it, and the padding species were named from memory and included one not in the format. the sweep that followed (3.92.0) settled the blast radius: the `.item`/`.ability` assignment surface across 238 files is clean (one hit, `noability`, the blank sentinel), so the hazard this item was written about never actually fired — but move literals hit five sites, two of them defects. `test-priority-block.js` silenced three slots with splash, which has no `mc.moves` row at all, so the silencing worked through absence rather than through the move doing nothing; and `test-dead-volatile.js` guarded on `.exists`, which is true for a banned move, so the guard could never fire and the case always ran on thousand arrows. tightening that guard would have moved the hole rather than closing it, so the subject is derived from the format (smack down). still open: `staged_board.js` and `game_differential.js` (`buildpair`)

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE ROSTER SCRIPT LANGUAGE HAS NO SWITCH ACTION, AND `board_state.js` DOES NOT COMPARE TRAPPING AT ALL. Will, 2026-08-10
open.full: the roster script language has no switch action, and `board_state.js` does not compare trapping at all. will, 2026-08-10: *"we need to test the switch blocking like shadow tag, block, and the trapping moves, so we need to be able to switch in the test"*. the roster says it in its own source at `tests/roster.js:1814`. two layers, and they must not be confused: the engine switches fine — measured, `{kind:'switch', to: body}` through `battleturn`, and a partial trap correctly refused it while the untrapped control left freely — but the roster drives through the differential's script language, which cannot express the action, and even if it could the comparator has no field for trapping. that is why `block` reads inert: nobody ever tried to leave. covers the hard-trap moves (block, mean look, spider web, anchor shot, thousand waves), the partial-trap family's switch-prevention half (chip damage was closed at 3.93.0; the trapping half has never been compared), and the trapping abilities

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE WEATHER-CONDITIONAL MOVE FAMILY, SWEPT. Nine moves in this format change behaviour with the sky. Verified CORRECT an
open.full: the weather-conditional move family, swept. nine moves in this format change behaviour with the sky. verified correct and now on record rather than assumed: thunder and hurricane are never-miss in rain and 50 in sun; blizzard is never-miss in snow and untouched by sun; solar beam and solar blade closed under the precondition layer. broken: `growth` does not double in sun (sd +2/+2, ours +1/+1) — it read match for months and went red the moment its precondition was real, which is the sharpest argument for the precondition work there is. open: only growth. a later sweep at release `f727f7fdee4f` closed the rest and this line is corrected rather than left standing: `weatherscaled` has eleven members and five payload shapes, growth is the sole member carrying a `boosts` payload, weather ball now reads match (#96's fix took), and the other nine — including electro shot, which this item wrongly called untested — are all green under `move/needs-the-sky-it-names`. the remaining untested weather surface is on the ability side: `solarpower`, `raindish` and `icebody` all read control-not-quiet. `dig` appears in a naive weather scan and is a false positive — its weather mention is `onimmunity` (underground bodies take no sandstorm or hail chip), a different mechanic, recorded here so the next sweep does not re-find it as a bug

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: FIVE TAG SIGNATURES ARE CARRIED BY MOVES THE ENGINE TREATS DIFFERENTLY — so something other than the tag is deciding, an
open.full: five tag signatures are carried by moves the engine treats differently — so something other than the tag is deciding, and 105,709 uses sit on those signatures. generalised from #126 rather than left as one anecdote: every move in `data/tags.json` was resolved through `playeraction` on the frozen release and grouped by its sorted tag list. five groups split on the resolved kind, and a split can only mean a name match (forbidden here) or a tag missing the param that should separate them (#71). ranked: 96,406 `protect`+`detect` -> `protect` but `endure` -> `affect`, the highest-usage signature in the format carrying three behaviours — and `protectmoves` is an exported name list, which is the mechanism; 4,924 `wideguard` -> a branch, `quickguard` -> nothing (#126); 3,721 `roost`/`recover`/`slackoff`/`softboiled` -> `heal` while `wish` and `rest` -> nothing, because the tag says *heals self* and cannot express delayed or also-sleeps; 524 `beatup`/`hex`/`storedpower` -> `attack`, `spitup` -> nothing; 134 `bellydrum`/`tidyup` -> `statcode`, `acupressure` -> nothing. the last three overlap #125's dead list and groups a/b of the 13-row diagnosis, so the fix is shared. the check itself is the deliverable — it is cheap, it is derived, and it should be a gate: a signature whose members resolve to different kinds is either a name match or an under-specified tag, and both are defects by this repo's own rules

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: 'GOOD ENOUGH' IS A USAGE-WEIGHTED THRESHOLD, NOT A ROW COUNT — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. Will
open.full: 'good enough' is a usage-weighted threshold, not a row count — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. will, 2026-08-10: *'we do have to ask ourelves at what point is the engine good enough and has enough used features that it can perform its end goal'*. measured against the corpus rather than argued: 553,910 total move clicks; 781 (0.14%) land on a move that resolves to a whole no-op turn; 3,888 (0.70%) land on a move the roster says disagrees with the authority; the union is 4,208 = 0.76%. so 99.24% of real clicks land on a move with no known defect, and the game differential is 150/150 clean on real replayed games. the gate is a coverage standard and has been read as a sufficiency standard. its 45 open move rows are deliberately-staged edge cases, which is precisely why they survived — they barely occur. the honest test of sufficiency is roadmap #68: scale the differential from 150 games to 1,000+ real stored games. if it stays clean there, the remaining rows are polish and can run beside search work rather than blocking it, and the #99 quarantine can lift on a measured condition instead of a feeling. note the standing counter-evidence, which cuts the same way: `docs/measure.md` §0 carries a tight null at n=8,883 on the hypothesis that correctness fixes move the leaf at all

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE OPTIMIZATION PASS — hand MEDICHAM to Fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch
open.full: the optimization pass — hand medicham to fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch cannot fake. will, 2026-08-10: *'once we think medicham is good enough i plan to run some optimization programs to speed it up'* / *'handing it over to feeble 5 and saying make this go faster'*. dispatchable directly — the model is selectable per agent. the hazard is that 'faster' and 'different' are indistinguishable to a benchmark. an optimizer that shaves 30% by skipping a branch produces a beautiful number and a broken engine, and every existing test can still pass because those tests cover mechanics the branch never touches. so the pass runs three instruments, not one: `tests/bench-medicham.js` for the score (built 2026-08-10, pinned fixture, best-of-5, refuses to record a baseline under load — first reading 0.4341 ms/turn); the 500-move x 4-turn whole-board digest sweep for the verdict (2,000 cells; wire 147 used it to show only 11 moved, and that is the shape every optimization must reproduce at zero); and `tests/test-damage-stages.js` at 1728/1728 exact so arithmetic shortcuts cannot drift. sequencing, which decides how much work this is: the classifier cascade is both the most likely optimization target and the thing the remaining ~20 wires append to. restructure it first and the queued fixes land in the restructured version; do the wires first and the optimizer rewrites code that was just written

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE COST OF A FEATURE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH PATH IT SITS IN, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10.
open.full: the cost of a feature depends entirely on which path it sits in, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10. will: *'how many of these features will slow down the engine? cause if it costs nothing to have harvest in there, then sure we can, but if there is a time cost to it then maybe we otta reconsider'* — the right question, and the answer splits cleanly. hot path — runs on every click of every rollout: the damage chain and the ~40-branch classifier cascade. tonight's five wires cost +6.2% (0.776 -> 0.825 ms/turn, interleaved a/b across frozen releases under load), and the per-hit damage loop is almost certainly all of it, being the only wire that touched damage. cold path — fires once per turn on a trigger, and is effectively free: harvest, cud chew, cheek pouch, quick guard, the heal family. so harvest specifically: yes, free. the thing to actually guard is compounding — 6% per five wires, twenty more wires, and the engine is ~25% slower to serve 0.76% of clicks. that trade stops being worth it well before the queue empties, which is the argument for #76's ratchet firing on every wire rather than at the end

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: A FEW MILLION SELF-PLAY GAMES TO PROVE THE SAMPLER FIRES AT THE RATE WE DECLARED — Will's idea, and the right tool for t
open.full: a few million self-play games to prove the sampler fires at the rate we declared — will's idea, and the right tool for the question it actually answers. *'once we feel our engine is good we can have it play a few million games and then determine if our rate for accuracy and secondary effects is right'*, then, on the distinction: *'correct run the million games after we determine'*. so: #132 first (is the declared number right — free, exact), then this (does the code fire at it — statistical). this catches the failure a probe structurally cannot: a probe forces the outcome to test the mechanic, so a secondary declared at 30% that a bug makes fire at 0% or 100% passes every probe and every roster row. that is claude.md's founding failure — a capability absent while everything reports success — in the one place the existing instruments are blind. cost is not a constraint: at the measured 0.4341 ms/turn and a mean 3.6-turn rollout, a million games is roughly half an hour. compare observed firing rates against the declared chances with a confidence interval per move, and expect the answer to be boring — the value is the one that is not

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE STORE REACHES FOUR FACTS AND THROWS THEM AWAY — and #68 needs every one of them. Will, reading the replay design: *'
open.full: the store reaches four facts and throws them away — and #68 needs every one of them. will, reading the replay design: *'i think multi hit moves say how many times they hit in the chat'*, *'life orb in the chat too'*, *'same with focus sash'*. all correct. `engine/durable-ingest.js` parses 30 protocol lines and drops these four: `|-hitcount|` (never read — so the differential skips 630 multi-hit rows as incomparable when the real hit count was on the wire); `|cant|` (never read — a flinched, paralysed, asleep, frozen or recharging body is simply an absent `m` event, indistinguishable from each other, 0 games in 52,089 carry a flinch marker); the `[from]` clause on chip damage — the parser tests for it to decide the damage is residual and then discards the text, so burn, sandstorm, life orb and rocky helmet all land as a bare `{t:'hp'}` with no source, and its own comment names them; `|-enditem|`, read only to infer what item a body held, never emitted as a turn event, so 'the focus sash triggered this turn' is gone. the store's event vocabulary is `b f fs hp m mega s w x`. this contradicts the project's founding principle — *store raw, analyze on top, every fact we might ever want* — at the parser. four regex arms; the raw replays can be re-pulled so no history is lost. ops work, touches no engine, and it makes #68 able to attribute a divergence instead of reporting an unexplained hp drop

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE SCENARIO CATALOGUE — one test SHAPE per mechanic, covering every move, ability, item and species. 920 entities carry
open.full: the scenario catalogue — one test shape per mechanic, covering every move, ability, item and species. 920 entities carry 217 distinct tags, so 217 shapes cover all of them and an entity added tomorrow inherits its shape without an edit; plus 357 legal species as one `structural` shape that needs no battle, only a comparison against the format. ten archetypes, and the archetype decides which instrument can ask the question — `chance` tags are marked so nobody builds a one-board test for a coin. two fields make it work and both are will's: `faces`, the adversary's action as distinct from the subject's precondition (*"wide guard needs a spread move against it, its pointless to test if it doesnt face that"*), without which a shape passes by doing nothing — and it explains the could-not-stage pile; and a property tested through its reactor (*"have contact hit rough skin to check"*), which resolves the `contact` flag's 166 moves in one shape. built by `engine/scenario_catalogue.js`, written to `data/scenario-catalogue.json`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE PP FACT HAS TWO READERS UNTIL ENGINE ADOPTS THE SHARED ONE. `medicham2-browser.js`'s `ppMax` / `ppLeft` / `ppDeduct`
open.full: the pp fact has two readers until engine adopts the shared one. `medicham2-browser.js`'s `ppmax` / `ppleft` / `ppdeduct` / `ppallout` / `pppressureextra` are file-local — on neither `module.exports` nor `root` — so `board.js` cannot call them, and #145 had to put the fact in `engine/pp.js` rather than copy it. that is claude.md's *"two files that both decide choice scarf is x1.5"* hazard, live. it is guarded rather than declared: `tests/test-pp-fact.js` plays real turns and asserts that the number medicham writes into its own `_pp` equals the number `pp.js` gives, across every maxpp tier in the format. the ask is one edit in engine's file — have those five delegate to `engine/pp.js`, or export them and let `pp.js` become a thin adapter — so that one implementation remains. two further items found while wiring. `board.js` writes `b._pp` by name, which ought to be an engine-supplied setter rather than a string literal in a consumer. and `docs/_outbox/pp-and-moldbreaker-notes.md` states that `floor(base*0.8)+4` fits 500 of 500 rows: it fits 499, because struggle carries `noppboosts` and stays at 1/1 where the formula gives 4. nothing downstream is wrong — the number is read, never computed — but the claim would have to break before the artifact did

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: TWO SHIPPED COMMITS CITE ROADMAP NUMBERS THAT WERE NEVER REGISTERED, AND A LATER AGENT REUSED THEM. Commits `0a28580` (4
open.full: two shipped commits cite roadmap numbers that were never registered, and a later agent reused them. commits `0a28580` (4.1.0) and `e7d672a` (4.2.0) name "roadmap #145" and "roadmap #146" in their messages and in `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md`. neither number existed in §5 — head's register stopped at #143. the search agent then correctly took #145 and #146 as the next free numbers for the pp work, so those two numbers now mean two different things depending on whether you read a commit message or the register. the findings are re-registered here as #147 (grounded axis) and #148 (sixth gate clause); the commit messages cannot be rewritten and are left alone, which is why this row exists. `tests/test-roadmap-register.js` did not catch it and is not wrong to have missed it — it checks that every item a division ledger schedules is named in §5, and these citations were in a commit message and the sprint notes, neither of which it reads. widening it to those two sources is the fix; until then a number in a commit message is not a registered number

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `status.js` STAMPS UTC WHILE EVERY DATED ARTIFACT USES LOCAL, SO ANY RUN AFTER 20:00 EDT IS DATED TOMORROW. Measured 202
open.full: `status.js` stamps utc while every dated artifact uses local, so any run after 20:00 edt is dated tomorrow. measured 2026-08-10 20:43 edt: `engine/medicham2-browser.js` has mtime `2026-08-10 20:41:29 -0400` and `docs/search.md`'s generated block renders it as `2026-08-11 00:40`. a changelog entry written in the same session was stamped `[4.4.0] — 2026-08-11` against a real date of the 10th and had to be corrected by hand. this is small and it is exactly the class this repository keeps paying for: an artifact that looks newer than it is, feeding a staleness comparison that then reads backwards. `engine/provenance.js` already had to stop comparing mtimes for this family of reason. fix: one date function, local, called by everything that stamps — the facts are global rule applied to the clock

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `data/status.js`'s GRAPH ROW NAMES THE WRONG BUILDER, WHICH IS WHY #153 WAS INVISIBLE. `engine/provenance.js` attributes
open.full: `data/status.js`'s graph row names the wrong builder, which is why #153 was invisible. `engine/provenance.js` attributes it to `engine/build-status.js`, which reads `policy-eval.json` and friends and is clear. the file's own header says it is generated by `build/build_status.js`, which reads two withheld artifacts — so the row that would have made `data/status.js` quarantined was never computed. two builders with almost the same name, one stale, and the graph followed the stale one. neither file may be deleted on this reasoning alone and web may not touch either; what is owed is a decision about which builder is live and a re-classification. related: `data/games.h2h-joint-trained.jsonl` and `data/games.h2h-tags2.jsonl` have no row at all, so doduo's and mew's evidence lines resolve to *unclassified* — the site withholds them on the ground that unclassified is not cleared, and that withholding expires by itself the day either file gets a row that clears.

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE CANONICAL SPEED BENCHMARK HAS NEVER HAD SIX BODIES, AND ITS STORED NUMBER WAS INVALID THE DAY IT WAS RECORDED — TYPE
open.full: the canonical speed benchmark has never had six bodies, and its stored number was invalid the day it was recorded — typed literal repaired 2026-08-27 by measure, re-record owed. `tests/bench-medicham.js` pinned `roster = [... 'amoonguss']`, a species that is `isnonstandard: 'past'` here and that `data/engine-data.js` has never carried — zero key hits on every commit that touched the file back to 2026-07-23, including `9a060821` on the day the benchmark was written. at the baseline commit `5884fd23` `buildmon` was `const m = monrow(name); if (!m) return null;`, and every game draws all six roster indices exactly once, so all 120 games ran with a null body on one side; `turns: 450` against a 120x12 cap is the fingerprint. `data/medicham-bench.json`'s 0.4614 ms/turn is withdrawn — it timed five bodies and a hole. today `monkey` throws (`engine/lookup.js`, armed 2026-08-02) so the file cannot run at all: the benchmark roadmap #76/#61 exists to provide has been dead and silent. repaired: the slot now holds toxapex, derived rather than picked — the highest team-rate legal, mc-carried, buildmon-safe body whose built set is majority-status, retains a damaging move and sits in the sub-56 speed tier amoonguss occupied (3.63% of teams / 1,554 games; regenerator, leftovers, infestation / toxic / wide guard / baneful bunker; `checklegal` legal, as are the other five). two guards added, both aimed at the exact failure: `mk()` throws on a null body instead of playing a hole, and the comparison refuses when `base.roster` differs from `roster` — the artifact has always carried the roster and nothing compared it, so the file's own "changing this list invalidates every stored number" was prose. owed: `node tests/bench-medicham.js --record` on a quiet machine. this batch may not play a game. until it is run there is no speed baseline for medicham and no optimization may claim a delta. report: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-typed-literals.md`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `g.sets` DUPLICATES EVERY MOVE THAT WAS BOTH DECLARED AND CLICKED, ON 97.96% OF THE CORPUS MAG IS FITTED ON — FILED 2026
open.full: `g.sets` duplicates every move that was both declared and clicked, on 97.96% of the corpus mag is fitted on — filed 2026-08-27 by measure, not fixed (engine/ops). on an open-sheet game the revealed set merges the sheet's move spelling with the log's spelling without normalising. printed rather than described, `gen9championsvgc2026regmbbo3-2653849509`: `g.sets.kangaskhan.moves = ["fakeout","lastresort","fake out","last resort"]` against a declared sheet of `["fakeout","lastresort"]`. measured: 84,761 of 263,859 bo3 revealed sets (32.12%) repeat a move id, in 20,370 of 20,795 games (97.96%); 90,531 sets carry more than four revealed moves, up to thirteen. `games.ots.jsonl` 16,695 of 52,964 sets (31.52%) in 99.23% of games. the control is exact: on the closed-sheet ladder the defect appears in 1,410 games and 1,410 of 1,410 carry a sheet, 0 do not, against 1,432 sheeted games in the store — so the sheet-merge path is the cause and nothing else is. it is not a legality bug and it shows up as one: it produces 200 of `games.bo3.jsonl`'s 221 `teamvalidator` move complaints and 43 of `games.ots.jsonl`'s 46, which is why the illusion signature reads 9.05% there against 86.8% on the ladder. the store stays raw — the repair is in the reveal path in `engine/durable-ingest.js`, not a rewrite of stored lines, and `engine/durable-ingest.js` is not measure's. until it lands, no measurement may read `g.sets[x].moves` on an open-sheet game as a moveset. whether the duplicate reaches mag's features is unmeasured and is downstream of the fix. report: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-bo3-unjudged.md`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: EIGHT COMMENTS NAMED A SOURCE FILE THAT IS NOT THERE — SIX CORRECTED 2026-08-27 BY MEASURE, TWO OWED BY ENGINE. A commen
open.full: eight comments named a source file that is not there — six corrected 2026-08-27 by measure, two owed by engine. a comment naming a repo `.js`/`.py`/`.html` file asserts that file exists. of 2,822 such references in `engine/`, `tests/` and `build/`, eight named something absent and did not say so (a negation within 200 characters clears it). this row as first filed said "not measure's to fix" and that was wrong about six of the eight — they sat in files measure owns; the misrouting is recorded rather than edited away. corrected, each repointed at what is actually true rather than deleted: `build/build_mag_data.js` said *"web/magnemite.html carries a self-check against a fixture generated here"* — 32 days, the worst; no such page has ever existed, the room is `roommagnemite()` and the check is `magselfcheck()`, both in `web/index.html`, and it detects a bundle-vs-engine vintage mismatch rather than two scorers diverging (the page stopped re-implementing `featuresfor` and calls `board.js` live, so the sentence was wrong twice). `engine/prior_player.js` *"see tests/test-policy-parity.js"* — 34 days, the oldest; no such test, and `setpurepriors()` in `engine/medicham2-browser.js` is the real switch and has no caller, so the like-for-like comparison has never been run. `engine/lookup.js` *"tests/test-lookup-contract.js reads this"* — 25 days (first written 2026-08-02, not the 21 days first reported); no such test, and `misses()` has no reader at all. `engine/million_run.js` *"engine/status_residual.js asserts it"* — 16 days; the identity guard is real and is the `if (dump_status)` block in that same file, which refuses to write on a mismatch. `engine/speed_vs_pokeenv.js` *"arm a lives in engine/bench_pokeenv.py"* — 16 days, printed to the operator at run time and written into `data/speed-vs-pokeenv.json`'s `what` field as a third arm that does not exist; arm a is unwritten and both now say so. `engine/quarantine.js` named `web/scoreboard.js` where `data/scoreboard.js` was meant — 13 days. still open, both in engine's files: `engine/game_differential.js` names `tests/rate_runner.js` (15 days; the instrument that derives its trials from statistical power is `engine/million_run.js`) and `engine/medicham2-browser.js` names `tests/test-engine-contract.js` (34 days; `tests/test-engine-consistency.js` is the file that holds the two engines together). re-derived on every run of `node tests/test-claim-truth.js`, which reports 2 of 2,822, down from 8. no engine byte moved and no game was played. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-false-claims.md`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: A CORPSE'S QUEUED ACTION IS RE-PRICED WITHOUT ITS PRIORITY ABILITY IN THE AUTHORITY, AND WHETHER WE DO THE SAME IS UNMEA
open.full: a corpse's queued action is re-priced without its priority ability in the authority, and whether we do the same is unmeasured — found 2026-08-27 by engine while closing #344. `getactionspeed(action)` re-derives a move action's priority every time the queue is resolved: `priority = runevent('modifypriority', action.pokemon, target, move, priority)` (sim/battle.ts:2643). `findeventhandlers` opens `if (target instanceof pokemon && (target.isactive || source?.isactive))` (:1053), and `faintmessages` has already set `isactive = false` on a body that died earlier in the turn (:2563) — so for a corpse that whole block is skipped and the event collects no handlers at all. measured, not argued: `tests/probe_corpse_in_slot.js` recomputes the skipped block on every call whose target is a corpse, over the pinned pool (129 pairs, release `f6a3b35ed665`, census pin `9446a684709d`). of the 13 event names that reach a corpse, this is the second and last one that suppresses anything: `modifypriority`, 4 corpse-calls, 2 suppressed handlers, both `galewings` (the other is `modifyspe`, which the 2026-08-27 replacement batch already landed). the control is the same recompute on live bodies: 267 of 6,493 sampled reads non-zero over 17 event names, so the 0s elsewhere are facts about the corpse. what is not measured, and the row says so rather than guessing. the corpse's action is refused at execution in both engines (`runaction` checks `!action.pokemon.isactive` and `action.pokemon.fainted`, :2703-2704), so a wrong priority on a dead action can only be observed if that action's position moves a live one — `battle#speedsort` is a selection sort whose swaps are a function of the whole list, the same mechanism roadmap #221 and `residualshadowsort` already model for the residual walk. nobody has measured whether medicham2 re-prices a dead body's queued action at all. it is rare and it is ranked as such (will 2026-08-23 — the pinned pool ranks, the census and roster carry the tail): 4 calls in 129 pinned-pool games, 2 of them carrying a handler. instrument owed: a fixture staging a gale wings body that dies with a flying move still queued beside a live speed tie, asserting the two engines put the surviving actions in the same order — with the knob in the direction that restores the priority, so an identical result across it says the knob is unwired.

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: QUICK CLAW'S EFFECT IS STILL GATED ON THE MOVE'S PRINTED PRIORITY AND THE AUTHORITY GATES IT ON THE EVENT'S RELAY VAR —
open.full: quick claw's effect is still gated on the move's printed priority and the authority gates it on the event's relay var — filed 2026-08-27 by engine while closing #497, counted rather than fixed. `data/items.ts` quickclaw is `if (priority <= 0 && this.randomchance(1, 5))`, and `priority` there is the first parameter of `onfractionalpriority`, which `runevent('fractionalpriority', action.pokemon, null, action.move, 0)` supplies as the relay var -- what an earlier handler in the same event returned, 0 on an ordinary claw holder. derived, not read: `tests/probe_fractional_priority_draw.js`'s highpri arm plays a priority-1 attack and the authority takes one `any` draw, against a noclaw control on the same board taking none. so the authority rolls and applies the claw above bracket 0. medicham2's `_fpok` refuses it there. #497 made the die agree on every move action; the outcome still does not, and `medfails.fracpriprioritygateunmodelled` is the size of the gap. two more clauses on the same line, also unmodelled and also counted: `quickclaw` returns before the roll when the move is status and the holder has mycelium might (`medfails.fracprimyceliumdrawunmodelled`), and the authority runs the ability handler (`onfractionalprioritypriority` -1) before the item's (-2) while this engine draws the item first -- under the relay reading that decides whether the claw rolls at all when a quick draw has already fired. not called a defect with a size until something measures it: the counters were added in the same commit and the population over the pinned pool was not read in that session. instrument owed: a fixture staging a claw holder clicking a priority-1 move where the nudge would change the order, with the knob in the direction that restores the refusal, so an identical result across it says the knob is unwired.

open.full: two ladder rows have a winner that is neither player, because the pre-2026-08-28 fetch split a multi-byte character across two http chunks. defect, store. filed 2026-09-09 by measure (`docs/_reports/2026-09-09-raw-shard-cap.md` §3). ids `gen9championsvgc2026regmb-2662690089` and `gen9championsvgc2026regmb-2672145722`: u+fffd sits only in the `|win|` line — the `|player|`, `|j|` and `|raw|` lines around it carry the correct bytes — the signature of `buffer#tostring` per chunk, which `engine/durable-ingest.js:43-62` records finding on 2026-08-28 and fixing with `setencoding('utf8')`. the extractor read the line it was given correctly; the line was wrong when it reached the raw store. showdown serves both replays clean today. fix: re-fetch and replace both the parsed row and the raw log; a raw shard is write-once, so the corrected raw log is a new shard and `--restore-raw`'s first-occurrence-wins must be reconsidered for a correction, or the correction lands in the plain archive with the old shard left as history. do not delete rows. the same defect left 194 raw logs carrying 496 u+fffd in nicknames and usernames (recorded in the `durable-ingest.js` header) — the same repair, wider. verified by: `engine/sanity_check.py` "the winner is always one of the two players" reads 2 → 0 on that repair and on nothing else.

open.full: future sight's payout draws no `acc` die where the authority draws one on a printed 100. defect, engine — die-count only, not a board one until an evasion stage is on the field. filed 2026-09-10 by measure from engine's batch y (`docs/_reports/2026-09-09-narration-batch-y.md` §9 row 2): measured 1 vs 0 addresses on the payout turn. under mode a every die is pinned on both sides, so a missing draw shifts every later roll in the game and shows up as a divergence attributed to whatever consumed the next die — which is why it is filed even though no board parts today. which accuracy path the authority takes for a `futuremove` payout is engine's to read from `data/conditions.ts`, not typed here. verified by: a probe staging the payout under an evasion stage on both engines, in `tests/test-mechanics.js` or a `tests/probe_*.js`, red then green.

open.title: RESIDUAL TIE ORDER FOLLOWS THE BODY LIST, NOT THE HANDLER LIST — THE brn / psn / LEFTOVERS TRIO IS ONE MECHANISM, AND TH
open.full: residual tie order follows the body list, not the handler list — the brn / psn / leftovers trio is one mechanism, and the record's "65/75, not a tie" was a base-speed read. defect, engine — narration on every measured game; board-material only in a mutual residual ko, which is unmeasured. filed 2026-09-10 by measure from engine's derivation (`docs/_reports/2026-09-10-residual-trio-derivation.md`); fix not applied — it is the next batch. mechanism: `residualorder` (`engine/medicham2-browser.js`) sorts every active body, fainted included, group by group; the authority sorts one flat list of residual handlers (`sim/battle.ts:492-507`, `speedsort` `:429-458`). under the differential's pin no tie die is drawn on either side (`engine/game_differential.js:1859` `o.tie = () => 0`; showdown's `shuffle` is the identity, asserted by the pin claims), so a tied pair's order is whatever each selection sort's swap history leaves, and the two lists differ whenever (a) a tied body also carries a lower-order handler — placing the order-5 leftovers group moves p1b's brn handler from index 1 to index 4, past p2b's — or (b) a faster body with no residual handler shares the field — overqwil at 127 (life orb) is not in the authority's list at all, but medicham's body sort selects it first and its swap carries scovillain ahead of umbreon. all three pairs are exact ties in built speed — 90/90, 117/117, 80/80 — read off the authority's `storedstats.spe` (a `speedsort` hook over three hooked config runs) and off `freshbodies(buildpair(sheet))`: `buildpair` assigns sp by slot index (+32 / +22 / +11 / 0), so umbreon (base 65, slot 0) and scovillain (base 75, slot 1) are both 117, and the "70/70, 60/60, 65/75 — two ties and one that is not" reading in batch s's hand list and the 2026-09-09 session-close record is retracted by that receipt. ruled out with the line that rules it out: a die at a different address (none exists under the pin); a wrong speed read (no scarf, paralysis, tailwind, unburden or stage in any card; `battle.ts:2811` refreshes `pokemon.speed` before `fieldevent('residual')`); trick room (no user on the field in any of the three; aside, champions negates speed under tr at `data/mods/champions/scripts.ts:46-51` where mainline uses `10000 - speed`); moody (the protocol agreed 61 lines through game 2's residual); sub-order (both members of each pair carry the same effect). related rows: #221 named the per-body walk on 2026-08-11 and closed it as one pass per order group; #422 named `residualorder`'s `array.prototype.sort` and left the residual site as narration — this row is what that site costs today. the engine's own header above `residualorder` states the limitation, and its justification ("a fresh key per call would let one tied pair come out one way at order 5 and the other way at order 9 — an order the authority cannot produce") is false: game 1 is that order under the pin, and under real dice `speedsort` shuffles per tied group. on release `489bea0577bc` the trio is 3 of the 7 remaining narration causes (`data/game-differential.json` `first_divergences`: `omit-protect …2660452545` t7 `brn<>brn`, `omit-spread …2636020596` t4 `psn<>psn`, `pair-protect-bust …2659228530` t7 `leftovers<>leftovers`). fix site: `residualorder` — extend the residual shadow (`residualshadowbuild/sort`, today built only when both sides carry the same side/field clock, `residualshadowneeded`) to body handlers so the walk is over the authority's list, or sort only the bodies holding a handler in the group being walked. which scoreboard: the lab moves (two probes green); the pool closes exactly three rows (narration 6 → 3 of 961) and board-material sits at 0 either way. verified by: `tests/probe_residual_trio_lower_order_handler.js` (red 2 of 4 on `7d66b526659e`; `none` and `lefto-on-p1a` controls green) and `tests/probe_residual_trio_handlerless_body.js` (red 2 of 4; `slow/slow` and `fast/slow` green) both green with the mechanism restorable by a knob, and the three `first_divergences` rows gone on a re-run under the same pins.

open.full: shed tail's `[weak]` refusal is written bare — the authority writes `\|-fail\|source\|move: shed tail\|[weak]` when the user is at or below half, and this engine writes `\|-fail\|source`. defect, engine — narration only; one more member of batch s's `-fail names the move` family (`tests/probe_fail_names_the_move.js`). filed 2026-09-10 by measure from engine's batch z (`docs/_reports/2026-09-10-narration-batch-z-substitute.md` §6). surfaced when the substitute fix let `pair-speedctrl …2654408616 vs …2654492165` play past its t2 substitute line: orthworm on 54/145 after a rock slide clicked shed tail; authority `\|-fail\|p1a: orthworm\|move: shed tail\|[weak]`, medicham `\|-fail\|p1a: orthworm`. authority `data/moves.ts:16166-16177` (`shedtail.ontryhit`, no champions override — `grep shedtail data/mods/champions/moves.ts` is empty): no ally to switch to → bare `-fail` (:16168); already behind a substitute → `-fail` + `move: shed tail` (:16172); `source.hp <= math.ceil(source.maxhp / 2)` → `-fail` + `move: shed tail` + `[weak]` (:16176). which of the three arms this engine handles today is engine's to read from the code, not typed here. it is batch z's changed-cause game — the one card that did not stop — and 1 of the 7 narration causes on release `489bea0577bc` (`data/game-differential.json` `first_divergences`, cls `-fail field 3`). verified by: a probe staging all three refusals on both engines, red then green; the `pair-speedctrl …2654408616` row gone on a re-run under the same pins.

open.title: THE DIFFERENTIAL'S `--dump-out` WITH AN ABSOLUTE PATH WRITES NOTHING AND EXITS 1 — AFTER THE WHOLE RUN HAS PLAYED. INSTR
open.full: the differential's `--dump-out` with an absolute path writes nothing and exits 1 — after the whole run has played. instrument, measure. filed 2026-09-10 by measure from engine's observation (`docs/_reports/2026-09-10-residual-trio-derivation.md` §3.1; batches y and z hit it too and wrote through a repo-relative `../../../appdata/…` path instead). `engine/game_differential.js:49` `d = (...p) => path.join(__dirname, '..', ...p)` is applied to `dump_out` at the `writefilesync` (`:9609`), so `c:\users\…\dump.json` becomes `abra\c:\users\…` and the write is enoent. it cost a step twice: a stale `dump-omit-protect.json` from an earlier agent's 21:05 run sat in the shared scratchpad and read as fresh output for two steps of the trio derivation. one-line fix, not applied that night because the file was another division's: `path.isabsolute(dump_out) ? dump_out : d(dump_out)`. from the same section, observed and not filed separately: `--dump-games` cards carry no speeds, so a speed-order divergence cannot be read from a dump alone — the trio needed a `speedsort` hook; and `lastsdlog()` is the raw log with private and public copies of every `\|split\|` line, so a probe that counts `-damage` lines must drop one (the instrument does at `:2440-2445`). verified by: `--dump-out <absolute path>` writes the file and exits 0, asserted by a selftest or `tests/test-game-diff.js`.

open.title: THE POOL PAIRING MOVED THREE TIMES IN ONE EVENING UNDER IDENTICAL FLAGS AND A FROZEN POOL — OBSERVED, NOT EXPLAINED. INS
open.full: the pool pairing moved three times in one evening under identical flags and a frozen pool — observed, not explained. instrument, measure — stated as observed; no cause is claimed. filed 2026-09-10 by measure from engine's observation (`docs/_reports/2026-09-10-residual-trio-derivation.md` §3.3). `--config x --games n --team-store data/team-pool-frozen --release 7d66b526659e` gave three different pairings on the evening of 2026-09-09 local (21:05 by the previous agent, 21:50, 22:05). what is known: `diff_swarm.buildswarm` picks every `step`-th team of those each config's predicate accepts; the predicates read live `data/tags.json`, which was regenerated at 20:53:59; and `data/diff-team-pool.json` was rewritten at 21:04:29. what is not known: which of those moved the sample, whether one of them did at all, or whether something else did. consequence already paid: the artifact's exact games could not be replayed from the live tree, so the trio (#563) was derived from slot-determined speeds and sheet-determined handler lists rather than from the games themselves. this is the shape `claude.md` already names for the live store (995 → 982 games an hour apart) arriving through a pool that is frozen — so `--team-store data/team-pool-frozen` is not sufficient on its own, and the receipt #547 fixed cannot see it because the pool bytes did not change. verified by: three runs under identical flags with `data/tags.json` and `data/diff-team-pool.json` held produce one pairing; or the mover is named and pinned by a flag or a digest stamped in the artifact.

open.title: `engine/replay_one.js` REPRODUCES A CORNER-PRIMARY RUN'S SCHEDULE WRONG, BECAUSE ITS WARM-UP ASKS `PRIMARY_ARM` AND NOT
open.full: `engine/replay_one.js` reproduces a corner-primary run's schedule wrong, because its warm-up asks `primary_arm` and not the run's primary. defect, instrument — small. filed 2026-09-10 by engine, not fixed. `engine/replay_one.js:187` reads `const isprimary = arm.id === g.primary_arm.id;` to decide whether to play the stones-removed control game before each measured one. `primary_arm` is `arms[0]` (`middle`), so replaying a game from a `--arm top-tie-first` run skips a control game per pair and the driver state the target game starts from is not the one it had on the night. it was harmless while a corner arm could not be primary (#569); it is not now. the tool already prints `no stored record ... unchecked` and writes no artifact, which is why this is filed rather than fixed in a measuring pass. owed: a `--run-primary <id>` flag defaulting to `primary_arm.id`, so an existing invocation is unchanged and a corner-primary replay can be asked for by name. verified by: replaying a known corner-arm game with the flag and getting reproduced against `data/divergence-turns.json`.

open.title: `Pokemon#useItem`'s `AfterUseItem` EVENT IS RAISED AT TWO OF THIS ENGINE'S SIX SPEND SITES AND NOT AT THE OTHER FOUR, SO
open.full: `pokemon#useitem`'s `afteruseitem` event is raised at two of this engine's six spend sites and not at the other four, so symbiosis does not answer a spent mental herb or a flung item. defect, engine — small, and the population is three legal carriers. filed 2026-09-10 by engine while wiring the item-disposition board leaf, not fixed. the authority runs `this.battle.runevent('afteruseitem', this, null, null, item)` unconditionally at `sim/pokemon.ts:1849`, at the foot of every `useitem` — and `data/abilities.ts` symbiosis is `onallyafteruseitem`, so the partner hands its item over on every non-berry spend, not only on an eaten berry. this engine reaches `passitemfromally` from `consumeberry` (the berry road), from `restorestatsupdate` (white herb) and from the focus sash branch of `consumesitem`. it does not reach it from `mentalherbcures`, from the fling spend in the update pass, from the power herb charge branch (unreachable in this regulation — the item is `isnonstandard: 'past'`), or from the non-berry branch of `berrycureupdate` (also unreachable today and already counted by `medfails.volatilecuredbynonberry`). so the live half is two sites: a spent mental herb and a flung item. `cs.abilitycarriers('symbiosis')` answers 3 legal carriers, so this is not an empty population. not smuggled into the batch that found it: 2026-09-10's item-disposition batch was a batch of one and was expected to move boards, so its effect had to be attributable to the leaf and to `recorditemused` alone. `recorditemused` deliberately records and does not announce or raise — its own header says so — and adding the event at four sites would have changed six measured line orderings in the same pass as a state fix. verified by: a staged mental herb spend beside a symbiosis partner holding an item, played on both engines, with the partner's item read after the spend — it must move on both. today no probe stages it.

open.title: DRAGON DARTS CANNOT BE STAGED THROUGH A 1v1 DAMAGE HARNESS — THE AUTHORITY'S OWN HIT LOOP THROWS. DEFECT, upstream — NOT
open.full: dragon darts cannot be staged through a 1v1 damage harness — the authority's own hit loop throws. defect, upstream — not a medicham defect and not patched here. filed 2026-09-10 by engine while wiring the multi-hit volley into `tests/test-engine-diff.js`. `move.smarttarget` is `true` in the dex for dragon darts and the three sites that clear it (`sim/battle-actions.ts:607`, `:634`, `:740`) all fire on a failure, so a click that succeeds keeps it. with one target the champions loop pushes a second entry into `movedamage` (`data/mods/champions/scripts.ts:521`) and writes `damage[1]`, and the emergencyexit sweep below it reads `targets[1].hp` on a one-element `targets` — `typeerror: cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'hp')`, reproduced on `dragapult dragondarts -> dragapult` and on `-> garchomp`. not patched: forcing `move.smarttarget = false` in the harness would be a differential editing the authority to get an answer out of it. it is counted and named instead — `data/engine-diff.json` `volley.unstageable`, 1 row of 6,000 — which is a smaller and honester skip than the 134 it replaces. owed: exercise the mechanic where a second body exists, i.e. confirm it is reached by `engine/game_differential.js` rather than assumed; a two-target damage reference is a different harness and is not proposed. verified by: `data/engine-diff.json` `volley.unstageable.dragondarts` — non-zero means still unstageable, absent means it became stageable.

last board of a finished battle only, so it cannot change a click. the authority, traced rather than argued (a `node -r` preload wrapping `fieldevent`/`singleevent`/`faintmessages` on `engine/replay_one.js`, every residual's handler sequence and every side/stall duration before and after): a perish-song expiry takes `fieldevent`'s duration-expiry branch, which `continue`s past `faintmessages()` (sim/battle.ts:519-523), so the walk runs one more handler — ticking it if it carries a duration — and that handler's `faintmessages()` (:565) ends the battle. three pool games on release `09b2b98feb98`, the only board-material corner games left after the speed-tie corner batch 1: top `…2654571284` t12 (reflect sub 1 ticks 2→1, light screen sub 2 stays 6; this engine read 5), bottom `…2634155984` t10 (tailwind ticks, raichu's stall stays; this engine lapsed the stall), bottom `…2662099996` t11 (a callback handler runs next and nothing ticks; swampert keeps `stall 1/c9`, this engine read 0). this engine keeps walking every remaining residual group and the foot-of-walk stall lapse, because `faintqueueowed()` holds both the group-top stop (`sidewiped(s)&&!faintqueueowed()`) and the stall hold open while the expiry's faint is still queued. a faithful fix is "exactly one more handler across group boundaries", which the group-major walk can only answer from `_res_shadow_list`; open.section: The paper
open.title: position against THREE comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. VGC-Bench (AAMA
open.full: position against three comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. vgc-bench (aamas 2026) — whose archive we already consume, and dropped from the fit for staleness (four days, mid-june, seven weeks old); `engine/corpus_shift.js` exists to measure the metagame distance and has never written an artifact. future sight ai — closed-source showdown bot, reportedly top 5% of the most popular format, matches revealed attributes to the most common set, ships a win-probability browser extension; also settles a naming question, since "future sight" is taken and this project names everything after pokémon. the pokeagent challenge (arxiv 2603.15563, neurips 2025, 100+ teams, two tracks) — by far the strongest reference of the three and not yet read. add sarantinos (arxiv 2212.13338, cambridge) as the closest published method: gen 7 random battles singles, peaked 33rd in the world, regret-minimisation opponent prediction, fills unknown properties from usage statistics, and explicitly rejects monte carlo sampling as too sample-inefficient — which is what miltank's leaf does. it also names our #29 independently: its first "biggest challenge" is keeping the team balanced, with a worked example that is the sack, and it asserts *"an ai agent cannot achieve this just by looking ahead with minmax or monte carlo tree search."* finally, its elo caveat is load-bearing for will's stated goal: comparing human and ai ratings is invalid unless they played each other — laddering with alakazam is exactly that, so the plan is sound and should say why
